units.name: Goals page
units.verdict: macOS desktop app (native GPUI, pointer and keyboard), single owner. Reviewed from 11 captures at 900x560, 1360 wide and 1728x1084, dark and light, plus the code. Nothing was driven live, because the browser can't reach a native app, so all keyboard and behaviour findings come from code. First impression: the page reads as organised. Rows, columns and shelves are clean, the type scale is calm, and the blue Continue button is the brightest spot. But the order doesn't serve the primary task. Rows sort by project then id, so needing attention changes neither a row's position nor its action. G1's question sits under an api goal, G4's failure is fifth, and every row but G3 offers Pause. Counts: 0 Catastrophe, 6 Major, 13 Minor, 4 Cosmetic. Top problem: the owner has to read all eight rows, then expand one, to find and act on what needs them (R2, R3). At the smallest window the attention text itself is truncated (R5). None of the fixes need an owner rule changed.

units.name: Goal run state and buttons
units.verdict: macOS desktop app, pointer and keyboard, reviewed for one owner running many agents. Evidence is 16 captures (15 dark at 1360x860, plus 900x560, 1728x1084 and one light) and the code: goal.rs, plus the goal/waves.rs, sidebar.rs, fmt.rs and taskboardd sources I traced from it. It is a native app with no page to open, so nothing was driven with real input. First impression: the page is calm and organised. The work dominates, waves read in order and How it runs stays quiet, so the problem is what the page says rather than clutter. Counts: 0 Catastrophe, 6 Major, 8 Minor, 3 Cosmetic. Top problem: the app doesn't reliably tell the owner which goals need attention. The Needs you badge stays at 1 while goals sit stopped, failed, held or short of their outcome (R8). The goal header never states the goal's state, and goal_state(), which holds all those labels, is only called from tests (R9). Close behind: Start on a paused or set-aside goal silently lifts the pause or brings the goal back (R10).

units.name: Goal header and menus
units.verdict: macOS desktop, pointer and keyboard. Reviewed at 1360x860, 1360x1500 and 900x560, in dark and one light capture, from 9 captures plus the source. The app is native, so nothing was driven with real input and the blurred-screen audit was not run. First impression: the header is calm and organised, with one clear blue action, a dominant title and a quiet readout, but it gets cluttered the moment a menu opens. Counts: 0 catastrophe, 4 major, 10 minor, 1 cosmetic. The top problem is R14: the button's tooltip stays up over its own open menu, hiding the button label, part of the first menu row and even the goal title. The most serious problem for the primary task is R16: a goal stopped for your review shows no sign of it in the header and offers only Pause. No fix here needs the owner's OK. 'Waits for you to press Start' is a seed effect and is not rated (see not_checked).

units.name: Goal waves and lists
units.verdict: macOS desktop app (GPUI, pointer and keyboard), reviewed from code and 8 dark captures at 1360 wide, 860 to 1500 tall. Nothing was driven live, and narrower sizes are computed from code. First impression, by eye only (the blur audit couldn't run): the page reads as organised, with calm cards, a clear wave order and quiet chrome. The weakness is that it shows the plan better than it shows what needs the owner now. Counts: 0 Catastrophe, 4 Major, 8 Minor, 4 Cosmetic. Top problem: a task that needs the owner leaves no trace on its wave card, and the list always opens at wave 1, so on a many-wave goal the page doesn't lead to the work that needs attention (R18). Close behind, task titles and agent questions are cut to about 148px at 1360 wide while the row spends 120px on 'Ships one PR' (R19), and below about 1050 wide the titles disappear (R20). 'Waits for you to press Start' traces to the extra seed's state (R121). No fix here needs an owner rule changed.

units.name: Goal aside: Attached, Notes, Devices, Bits
units.verdict: macOS desktop, pointer and keyboard. I reviewed the Goal page's right column from six dark captures (1360x860 and 1360x1100) and the code: attached.rs, lists.rs, pool.rs, goal.rs, kit.rs and app.rs. I didn't run the native app, so nothing was used with real input. Blurred, the page reads as organised: the wave cards dominate and the aside is a calm single card with clear sections. The aside's problems are about priority and truth, not clutter. Counts: 0 Catastrophe, 1 Major, 10 Minor, 3 Cosmetic. The top problem is that nothing in the aside can be reached from the keyboard: the app has no tab stops at all, and file previews exist only on hover. The top design problem is Attached, where the Wave 2 picker sits above files that aren't in Wave 2, so the numbers on screen (4 of 7, All waves 5, Wave 2 2) never add up. L2 is met: waves use a pop-up menu. L1 is met for tasks, but the GOAL group's files aren't indented. No fix below needs an owner rule changed, except keeping the Jira control in R84.

units.name: Projects page
units.verdict: macOS desktop, pointer and keyboard; a native GPUI app. Reviewed at 1360x860 and 1360x1100 in dark from 5 captures, plus code for the other window sizes, light theme, keyboard and failure states. The app could not be driven, so nothing was used with real input. First impression, judged by eye from the captures because the blur audit could not run: the page reads as organised and calm, with a clear list, header and cards, and the orange Needs you pills are the only warm spots. Its order does not serve the primary task, though. Goals sort by group, then newest id, so what needs the owner lands mid-list, and the project list is alphabetical. Counts: 0 Catastrophe, 5 Major, 10 Minor, 2 Cosmetic. Top problem (R23): nothing on the page ranks by attention, and the page opens on the first project by name even when another one needs the owner. R24 and R25 compound it: a Needs you pill gives no reason or action, and the project list can disagree with the goals it summarises.

units.name: Flow 2: Run a goal
units.verdict: macOS desktop app (pointer and keyboard), reviewed at one size only: 1360x860, dark, expanded width. Evidence was 10 captures, the two named code files, and the app and daemon source they call. No running app was reachable, so I used no real input and ran no blur or `inspect`. First impression: the goal page reads as organised. The work dominates, the header is quiet, and a planned goal gets one clear blue Start. The happy path to Start is sound; the weak part is what comes after it. Counts: 0 Catastrophe, 4 Major, 10 Minor, 0 Cosmetic. The top problem is on a paused goal: the header still offers blue "Start 1 more task" beside blue "Resume the goal". That Start silently unpauses the whole goal while its toast mentions only one queued task. Pause also removes the goal from the sidebar while its tasks still run. Resume then confirms with a stale "Paused" toast and a "Going again" note that never clears.

units.name: Flow 3: Wave stop
units.verdict: macOS desktop app (GPUI, pointer and keyboard), reviewed from 11 dark captures at 1360×860 and 1360×1240 plus the Rust code. I didn't run the app, and no browser page applied, so the audit, inspect and real-input passes were not run. First impression from the captures: each surface reads as organised and calm, with the work dominant. The flow's problem is coverage, not clutter: the three kinds of stop are not treated alike. A review stop is handled well: it is noticed in sidebar, Needs you and Goals, and it releases from all three. A failed task is missing from Needs you, can't be released from its Goals row, and the sidebar words it like a review stop. A held wave shows nowhere outside the goal page. The owner has to open each goal to find it, and the Needs you badge can read nothing while goals stand still. Counts: 1 Catastrophe, 4 Major, 8 Minor, 1 Cosmetic. Top problem: R1, a held wave stalls its goal silently. 'Waits for you to press Start' is a seed effect and is not rated: `waits_for_start` is true only for manual pickup in a goal with no `ran_at`.

findings.title: A held wave shows nowhere outside the goal page
findings.element: Sidebar › Active goals › G5; Needs you; Goals › G5 row, at 1360×860 and 1360×1240, dark, held wave
findings.problem: G5 is stopped until the owner acts, yet the sidebar reads a plain '1 of 2', Needs you has no row, and the Goals row reads 'Queued' with Pause, the same as a healthy waiting goal (r-needs.png, r-goals.png). Only the goal page says 'Held' and offers the release (r-g5.png). In code, `stopped_line` returns None for a held wave, so `goal_sub`, `stop_vm` and `goal_row` all stay silent. Anyone can hold a wave (waves.rs, including `tb goal wave --hold`), so the owner may not know it happened. The only other signs are the 'Held' meta in the row's expanded wave list and, after 2 hours, an amber 'last update' time, which says stale rather than held.
findings.principle: Visibility of system status [NNG-H1]; walkthrough question 2, will users notice the action is available [NNG-CW]
findings.fix: In taskboardd/waves.rs, make `stopped_line` return 'Wave 2 is held' when the first unpassed wave has `held == true`, and extend `stopped_wave` so `stage_entry` emits a stage for it. In `stop_vm`, read the wave from `stage.wave` rather than parsing ' is done'; title 'Audit log · wave 2 held', act Continue with the label 'Let wave 2 start'. In `goal_row`, set now to 'Wave 2 held' in St::Needs, next to '1 task waits', and offer the same action in place of Pause. In `goal_sub`, show '1 of 2 · wave 2 held'. It lands under Decide, so the agents-only count doesn't change.

findings.title: In-progress rows aren't ordered or marked by what needs attention
findings.element: Goals › In progress list, all sizes and both themes (r-goals.png, r-goals-light.png, r-goals-small.png, r-goals-large.png)
findings.problem: in_progress() sorts by project then id, so a working api goal (G14) leads, G1 (needs you) is 2nd, G3 (stopped for review) is 4th, G4 (failed) is 5th and G13 (held) is last. All cards look the same; only one line of coloured text differs. At 900x560 about four and a half rows fit, so with more goals an urgent row can sit below the fold. The sidebar lists the same goals in a different order (G14, G13, G6, G5...), so position can't be learned either.
findings.principle: Primary content first, squint test [SCR-2] [NNG-VH]; Recognition rather than recall [NNG-H6]; Flexibility and efficiency [NNG-H7]
findings.fix: In in_progress(), sort into stable bands, then by id: needs you or stopped for review, failed, held (R4), working, in review, queued. St::rank() already gives most of this order. The project chip stays on each row, so project sort isn't lost. Give rows in the top two bands a quiet marker: card border in t.warn_line or t.down_line, or a 3px left edge in the status colour. Don't add a new section or labels. Use the same order in the sidebar's Active goals.

findings.title: Rows that need the owner offer Pause, not the action that moves them
findings.element: Goals › In progress › row action, G1 and G4 (r-goals.png, goals.png)
findings.problem: goal_row() always gives Pause unless a wave is stopped. G1 says 'T3 waits on your answer' but its only button is Pause, and that text isn't clickable. To answer, the owner must expand the row, find the row and press Answer (r-goals-expand-all.png). G4 failed and also only offers Pause. Eight near-identical buttons make the row's one strong control the least useful one, and a misclick pauses the goal that was waiting on you.
findings.principle: Cognitive walkthrough Q2, Q3 [NNG-CW]; one primary action [NNG-H8]; Frequent in view, rare behind [SEC-8]
findings.fix: Extend Action with Answer(task ref) and Open(task ref). When the tally has a Needs task, the slot shows 'Answer T3' and calls m.open_task, using the same right panel as the task row. When a task failed, show 'Open T54'. Keep Continue as it is. Show Pause only on rows with no owner action. Pause stays on the goal page for the other rows.

findings.title: A goal held back from finishing just says 'Done' and offers Pause
findings.element: Goals › In progress › G13 Replay every error (r-goals.png, r-goals-large.png)
findings.problem: G13 shows 1 of 1, a full green bar and 'Done', yet it stays In progress with Pause. goals.rs only leaves a goal unfinished if bits are waiting, an outcome missed, a failure is unaccepted or a PR is open. now_line() knows none of this and falls through to 'Done'. The owner sees a finished goal in the wrong list and can't tell it is blocked, though the goal page already has the words ('Waiting on 1 bit'). The exact reason in this seed wasn't checked.
findings.principle: Visibility of system status [NNG-H1]; Help users diagnose [NNG-H9]; Walkthrough Q4 [NNG-CW]
findings.fix: When every task is settled but the goal isn't finished, use the goal page's state instead of 'Done': 'Waiting on 1 bit' or 'Outcome not met' in St::Needs colour, with the reason on the second line. Reuse goal_state from goal/pool.rs. Rank it in the attention bands (R2), and drop Pause, since nothing is left to pause.

findings.title: At the smallest window, truncation removes the attention text
findings.element: Goals › In progress rows at 900x560, dark (r-goals-small.png)
findings.problem: The row keeps the same five columns at every width, so all of them shrink together. '1 working · 1 need…', 'Stopped for your r…', 'T3 waits on your answ…', 'Sign-in with…', 'Checkout on…' and 'Wav…' are all cut. The words that say a goal needs you are the ones lost, while 20px gaps, the 110px action column and the chevron column stay fixed. Opening the right task panel likely narrows the page further (not captured).
findings.principle: Every control at every size, narrowing keeps the order [SCR-6]; window reflow [HIG-MACOS]
findings.fix: Below about 800px of page width, switch goal_head to a compact layout. Name column takes the full width on line 1 with ref and chip. Line 2 is the status line at full width. Progress becomes a 96px bar plus '1 of 4', and the wave text is dropped from the row because it is in the open body. Reduce row gap from 20 to 12. Never truncate row.now before row.name: give it flex_none up to its text width.

findings.title: Nothing on the Goals page can be reached from the keyboard
findings.element: Goals › every row, ref, Pause, Continue, Answer, Open PR, Expand all, Collapse all, shelf line, earlier link
findings.problem: goals_page.rs and kit's buttons have no focus handle, tab stop or key handler; MainWindow holds the only page-level focus. There is no Tab order, no visible focus, and rows can't be opened or Continue pressed without a pointer. Cmd-number navigation and the project picker's own arrows work, but the primary task doesn't. Found by reading code; Tab wasn't pressed in the app.
findings.principle: Keyboard [WCAG 2.1.1]; Focus visible [WCAG 2.4.7]; Arrows within groups [MS-KBD]
findings.fix: Give the list one tab stop with roving selection: Up and Down move a visible selected row (2px t.accent ring), Right or Enter opens it, Left closes it, Cmd+Down opens the goal page. A key for the row's action, such as Space, runs Answer, Continue or Pause. Add focus handles to kit::btn so buttons take Tab and Space. Bind through the existing MainWindow key context.

findings.title: Shared tasks count in the total but aren't listed or tallied
findings.element: Goals › G2 Faster sign-in, folded and open (goals.png, r-goals-open.png)
findings.problem: G2 says '2 of 7', but the open row lists six tasks and the bar has six units. The summary's total uses counted_tasks (own plus shared). The detail's 'tasks' holds own tasks only, and shared cards arrive in a separate 'shared' key that goal_body, Tally::of and next_line never read. The owner can't find the seventh task. Worse, a shared task that needs you drops out of the row's status once details load, while the goal page does show it. This isn't the known Projects issue.
findings.principle: One fact, one place [SEC-7]; Visibility of system status [NNG-H1]
findings.fix: Read tasks and shared together, as goal.rs:122 already does, in Tally::of and next_line. In goal_body, add a 'Shared' section after 'No wave' with the same task_row, as goal/waves.rs does.

findings.title: Needs you and the sidebar miss goals that are waiting on the owner
findings.element: Sidebar › Needs you badge and Active goals rows, all extra-seed captures (r-g3.png, r-g4.png, r-g5.png, r-g13.png), dark, 1360x860
findings.problem: The badge reads 1 while G3 waits for a review, G4 has a failed task, G5 is held and G13 missed its outcome. Rows are no better: the orange dot only shows for needs > 0, so G4 ('stopped for you') has none. G5 reads a plain '1 of 2'. G13 reads '1 of 1' under a full green bar, which looks finished. The owner scanning the sidebar concludes one thing needs them. Code: waiting_count() counts only tasks in needs with question or attention, plus gone-quiet alerts, so stage items on the Needs you list are left out. goal_sub() has no held or miss branch.
findings.principle: Visibility of system status [NNG-H1]; one fact, one place [SEC-7]; the brief's primary task is seeing which goals need attention
findings.fix: Add stopped stages to the count the badge reads, so it matches the Needs you list: add stopped, non-resting goals to waiting_count(), or give the badge its own count if the agent count must stay. Show the dot when needs > 0, or when stopped is set, a wave is held or misses > 0. Extend goal_sub(): '1 of 2 · wave 2 held', '1 of 1 · 2 misses', '1 of 3 · T54 failed'. Paint a miss as a warn segment at the end of the sidebar bar, or at least stop it reading as all green.

findings.title: The goal header never says what state the goal is in
findings.element: Goal page › header and progress line, all states; clearest in r-g3.png, r-g4.png, r-g5.png, r-g10.png
findings.problem: Nothing at the top says 'Waiting on you', 'Held' or 'Done'. r-g5.png reads '1 of 2 done · 1 queued', which sounds healthy. r-g10.png only implies finished through '2 of 2 done', with no finish time. In r-g3.png, r-g4.png and r-g5.png the one header control is Pause, whose tooltip says running tasks carry on, on a goal that has already stopped with 0 terminals in use. The real action sits in a wave card, which can be well down a long goal: in goal-g2.png the wave 3 stop sits under two other cards. goal_state() has all these labels, but only tests call it, despite its comment saying the Goals list shows it.
findings.principle: Visibility of system status [NNG-H1]; squint test [SCR-2]; walkthrough question 2, will users notice the correct action
findings.fix: Render goal_state() as a tone-coloured chip in the ref and project row of header(): 'Waiting on you', 'Held', 'Done', 'Blocked', 'Outcome not met'. Add a Held case. First fix a bug in it: line 129 returns 'Done' with tone up when every task has status done, even if one has failed, so check b(t,'failed') before returning Done. For a finished goal, add the finish time next to it, as 'Done 6:25 PM'. Hide Pause while the goal is stopped at a gate with nothing running.

findings.title: Start on a paused or set-aside goal silently undoes the pause or brings it back
findings.element: Goal page › header Start button beside the gate banner, g2-paused.png and r-g9.png
findings.problem: Two blue buttons compete. The banner says 'Nothing new starts', yet 'Start 1 more task' or 'Start' sits above it. The tooltip only says it queues planned tasks, but POST goals/:g/run also clears paused and deprioritized (api.rs line 2853). One click meant for one task sets the whole goal running, and the toast only says 'Started: 1 task queued'. With no planned tasks, a header 'Resume' sits beside the banner's 'Resume the goal', and the two differ: only the header one also resumes parked tasks.
findings.principle: Consistency and standards [NNG-H4]; error prevention [NNG-H5]; one emphasis [SEC-5]
findings.fix: In run_buttons_view, push no run button while gate_view(g) is Some, so the banner holds the only primary action. Send Resume through goals/:g/run, or make the banner's call also resume parked tasks, so there is one meaning. If Start stays on a paused goal, label it 'Resume and start 1 more task' and say so in the toast, and do the same for a set-aside goal with 'Bring back and start'.

findings.title: A chained goal looks exactly like one waiting for Start
findings.element: Goal page › header and How it runs, r-g8.png compared with r-g7.png
findings.problem: G8 runs after another goal, but its page shows nothing about that: same primary Start, same How it runs as an ordinary planned goal. goal.rs never reads after or after_blocker; only the Goals page, Projects and the sidebar line do, and a chained goal is in the Next group, so it isn't in the sidebar. Start can't start it early either: the tasks queue and hold until the earlier goal finishes (test a_chained_goal_run_early_holds_its_tasks), and the board runs it anyway once that goal finishes. The owner is told to press something that isn't needed and can't do what it says.
findings.principle: Visibility of system status [NNG-H1]; walkthrough question 3, does the label match the result
findings.fix: When after_blocker is set, replace primary Start with a quiet non-primary label 'Starts after G7', with a link to that goal. Add a How it runs row: 'Runs after  G7 Search rewrite'. Keep the caret menu for a set time only if a scheduled start can really go ahead of the chain; otherwise drop it.

findings.title: The failed gate offers only the bypass, and no way to retry
findings.element: Goal page › Wave 1 gate, r-g4.png
findings.problem: 'T54 failed. Wave 2 waits.' has one button, blue 'Continue anyway', which skips the failure with no confirmation and no word on what wave 2 will inherit. The backend's own text says 'Try again, or continue past it', but the row's Try again only appears for start failures (start_failed), not failed work. The only retry is in the task panel, so the owner must know to open the row. The failure reason is cut to 'The bucket refused the uplo…' at 1360, right where it's needed.
findings.principle: Help users recognize, diagnose and recover from errors [NNG-H9]; error prevention [NNG-H5]; one emphasis [SEC-5]
findings.fix: In the failed gate, make 'Try again' the primary button, with the same requeue signal the panel uses (one failed task; 'Try again all' for several). Make 'Continue anyway' secondary, with a tooltip: 'Wave 2 starts without T54's work'. Show the reason on its own line in the gate, up to 2 lines, instead of relying on the truncated row cell.

findings.title: At the smallest window, task titles disappear
findings.element: Goal page › wave rows and wave header, g2-small.png, 900x560
findings.problem: How it runs keeps its width and the wave cards shrink to about 235 pt. The rows' fixed columns need about 370 pt (status 92, ref 36, PR 120, age 44, plus padding and gaps), so titles and reason lines get no room. Rows show only 'Done T6' and 'Queued T9', the PR column is cut at 'Ships on', and 'Review stop after this wave' is cut to 'Re'. The owner can't tell tasks apart. A gate's text and button would have the same width; that is Likely, as no gate was captured at this size.
findings.principle: Every control at every size; the work stays the biggest thing [SCR-1] [SCR-6] [NNG-H8]
findings.fix: When the main column is under about 900 pt wide, move the aside below the waves at full width, or fold it to a How it runs line. Under about 520 pt per card, drop the PR column and age from rows so titles keep at least 180 pt. Let the review-stop pill wrap below the wave title instead of being clipped.

findings.title: The tooltip covers the menu it belongs to
findings.element: Goal › header › Start caret, scheduled button, waiting button, at 1360x860 dark, menu open (g2-start-menu.png, r-g7-start-menu.png, r-g12-menu.png, r-g6-hours-menu.png)
findings.problem: With the pointer still on the button, its tooltip draws over the open menu. In r-g12-menu.png it hides most of 'Starts tomorrow at 1:55am' and touches the 'Start now' row. In r-g6-hours-menu.png it hides the 'Waiting until' label and part of the goal title. In g2-start-menu.png it cuts across Pause and Open in Claude. This happens on the menus that start work, and each tooltip only repeats what the menu already says.
findings.principle: Hover content must not obscure the task; every element earns its place [WCAG 1.4.13] [NNG-H8] [SCR-2]
findings.fix: In buttons() (goal.rs:970-1015), attach the tooltip only while that button's menu is closed, for example .when(m.menu_open(SCHED_MENU).is_none(), |b| b.tooltip(...)). Do the same for START_MENU on goal-run-caret and WAIT_MENU on goal-wait. Also keep it closed when the menu is dismissed, until the pointer leaves and comes back.

findings.title: Header buttons and menus can't be used from the keyboard
findings.element: Goal › crumbs, header buttons, Outcome not met, all menu rows, at every size
findings.problem: Start, Pause, Open in Claude, the crumbs and every menu row are mouse-only. The app source has no tab_index or tab_stop, and track_focus appears only on the root, text fields and a few panels. Esc closes a menu, and the Start at field does take focus, type and submit, but the only way to reach that field is a click. Rated 3 rather than 4 because the owner works with a pointer and `tb start` exists outside the app.
findings.principle: All functions work from the keyboard; arrows move inside menus [WCAG 2.1.1] [MS-KBD] [WCAG 2.4.7]
findings.fix: Give kit::btn, kit::link and the crumb links a FocusHandle with tab_index(0), a visible 2px accent focus ring, and Enter and Space activation. In menus, move focus to the first row on open, use Up and Down between rows, Enter to run, and return focus to the trigger on Esc. Add a goal-page shortcut for the primary action, for example Cmd+Return for Start. Open the menu from the button's bounds, not e.position(), so a keyboard open lands in the right place (see R58).

findings.title: A goal stopped for your review looks like a running goal in the header
findings.element: Goal › header › buttons and progress readout, stopped goal G3 (r-g3-light.png, r-g3-small.png)
findings.problem: The header reads '2 of 4 done · 2 queued' and offers Pause, which suggests the goal is moving and might need slowing. In fact nothing will happen until you press 'Continue to wave 2', and that button lives inside a wave card that scrolls. The owner's main question is which goals need them, and the header doesn't answer it. On a goal stopped at a later wave the action would likely start below the fold (Likely, not captured). The same state also has three names: 'stopped for you' in the sidebar, 'waiting for your review' on the wave, and 'Review stop' in How it runs.
findings.principle: Visibility of system status; the correct action must be noticeable [NNG-H1] [NNG-CW] [SEC-8]
findings.fix: When a wave is held for review, add a branch to gate_view so the existing pinned gate banner shows: label 'Waiting for your review', text 'Wave 1 is done. Look it over, then let wave 2 start.', button 'Continue to wave 2'. Remove the same banner from the wave card so the action has one home. Hide Pause in this state, since nothing new can start. Append ' · waiting for your review' to the readout in warn_text, and use that one phrase in the sidebar too.

findings.title: At the smallest window the aside squeezes the work until task titles disappear
findings.element: Goal › body under the header, 900x560 dark (r-g3-small.png)
findings.problem: The wave column shrinks to about 234px while How it runs keeps about 330px, so the secondary panel is wider than the work. Task rows show only 'Done T49' with no title, the wave heading cuts off at 'waiting for y', and the review banner wraps to one or two words per line beside its button. The pinned header also takes about 190 of 560px. This sits just below the header, but it is in the supplied capture and holds the action a stopped goal needs.
findings.principle: The work dominates; narrowing keeps the order [SCR-1] [SCR-6] [HIG-MACOS]
findings.fix: When the main area is under about 760px wide, stack the aside below the waves (or collapse it to a 'How it runs' row with Show), so the waves get the full width of about 580px at 900. Let the banner use flex_wrap with the button on its own line below the text. Keep the task title as the last column to give up space: hide the status line and 'Ships one PR' first.

findings.title: Wave cards hide which wave needs the owner
findings.element: Goal page › wave list › card headers and opening scroll position, any goal with several waves (r-g6.png, g1-needs.png)
findings.problem: The header dot and meta come only from the wave's own state (waves.rs head()), so a running wave holding a 'Needs you' task still shows a blue dot and 'Now'. The list opens at the top with finished waves first and has no way to jump. r-g6.png needs 1500px of height to show nine one-task waves, so at 860 tall the later waves are off screen. The header says '1 needs you' but gives no route to that row. In g1-needs.png, with no waves, the two Needs you rows are split by Done and Working rows. No capture shows a needs task inside a wave; that case is proven from code.
findings.principle: Visibility of system status [NNG-H1]; recognition rather than recall [NNG-H6]; frequent in view, rare behind [SEC-8]
findings.fix: Add a needs count to Head: when any row in the wave is St::Needs or St::Failed, use that dot and append '1 needs you' to the meta in t.warn_fg. On opening a goal, call ListState::scroll_to on the first card with a needs or failed row or a gate, falling back to the running wave. Fold runs of finished waves into one row ('Waves 1–6 done'), expanding inline. If a jump control is wanted, make it a pop-up menu like Attached's wave menu, not tabs (L2).

findings.title: Titles and questions are cut while the row reserves space for little
findings.element: Goal page › wave cards › task row, 1360 wide (g1.png, g1-needs.png, r-g6.png, goal-g2.png)
findings.problem: The row's fixed parts take 382px of 692px. The remaining 310px splits 1 : 1.1 with flex-basis 0, so a title gets about 148px whatever its neighbour holds, even when the status line is empty. Results: 'Add the WebAuthn regi…', 'Settings page: manage…', 'Re-measure and comp…'. The line that matters most reads 'Question: Should removing t…', and the full text is only in a hover tooltip. Meanwhile the PR column spends 120px on 'Ships one PR' on nearly every open row, which tells the owner nothing.
findings.principle: Everything earns its place [SCR-5]; aesthetic and minimalist design [NNG-H8]; owner rule: no filler labels
findings.fix: In row_el, leave out the line cell when x.row.line is empty so the title takes its width, and change the split to title 1.6 : line 1. In pr_cell, return an empty string for the default 'Ships one PR' and show only real facts (PR number, branch, 'No PR'); when no row in a card has a PR value, drop the column for +132px. For loud rows (questions), put the line on a second row under the title at 56px height. The list measures each item, so virtualization still holds.

findings.title: The wave list has no narrow layout, and titles vanish below about 1050 wide
findings.element: Goal page › body (lists.rs body()) › wave list and aside, windows from the 900×560 minimum to about 1260 wide
findings.problem: The sidebar (248px) and the aside (330px plus a 16px gap) never give way, and nothing in ui/goal reads the window size. Computed from the code, and the same sum gives the 148px title measured at 1360: a 900-wide window leaves a 232px card for 382px of fixed row parts. Title and status line get 0px, and the card's overflow_hidden cuts off PR and age. Titles reach 0px at about 1050 wide and stay under 100px until about 1260. Not rendered, because no capture is narrower than 1360.
findings.principle: Windows can be resized and the layout reflows across the whole range [HIG-MACOS]; narrowing keeps the order [SCR-6]; desktop window range (pass 7)
findings.fix: Add width steps to lists::body. Below 1200 wide, move the aside under the waves as extra list items, or into a pop-up, so the list takes the full width. Below 760 of list width, hide the PR column and then the age. Keep chip, ref and title always, with a title minimum of 160px.

findings.title: Task rows and findings can't be used from the keyboard
findings.element: Goal page › task rows, Plan review rows, Try again and gate buttons, all sizes
findings.problem: waves.rs, review.rs and lists.rs set no track_focus, key handler or focus style, and no tab_index or tab_stop appears anywhere under ui/. A row opens only by mouse click and a finding unfolds only by mouse click, so the owner can't arrow through tasks and read each in the panel, and no focus indicator exists. backlog.rs already has a focused list with a key handler. Whether kit buttons take focus by another route wasn't traced.
findings.principle: Keyboard [WCAG 2.1.1]; focus visible [WCAG 2.4.7]; arrow keys move inside groups [MS-KBD]
findings.fix: Give the wave list the backlog.rs pattern: track_focus plus on_key, with Up and Down moving a marked row (2px t.accent outline), Return opening it with m.open_task, and the panel following the selection while it's open. In Plan review, Return or Right opens a finding and Left folds it. Make the gate button reachable with Tab.

findings.unit: Goal aside: Attached, Notes, Devices, Bits
findings.title: No aside control can be reached or used from the keyboard
findings.element: Goal page › aside › wave picker, kinds menu, file rows, task labels, Show/Hide, Focus, device holder links, issue rows, both menus; all sizes
findings.problem: A search of taskboard-app/src finds no tab_index, tab_stop or .focusable(, so Tab can't land on any of these controls. The wave and kinds menus take no arrow keys; Esc closes them (app.rs escape) but they can only be opened with a click. Image previews and the file's name, date and summary appear only in a hover card, so those have no non-hover route.
findings.principle: Every function works from the keyboard, with a visible focus state [WCAG 2.1.1] [WCAG 2.4.7]; arrows move inside groups and menus [MS-KBD]; hover is never the only path [desktop:HIG-POINTER]
findings.fix: Give menu_btn, wave_btn, fold_toggle, file_row, the task label and issue_piece a FocusHandle with tab_stop(true) and a 2px t.accent focus ring, and make Enter and Space run their click. When a menu opens, move focus to its selected row; Up and Down move, Enter picks, Esc closes and returns focus to the button. Show the hover card on focus too. Add F6 to jump between the wave list and the aside.

findings.title: Work that needs you is not first, in the goals or in the project list
findings.element: Projects › Active card, Tasks card and project list, all sizes (projects.png, r-projects-open.png, r-projects.png)
findings.problem: In projects.png, G2 Working sits above G1 Needs you. In r-projects-open.png, G13 Planned, G6 Queued and G5 Queued come before G4 and G3 Needs you, and G1 Needs you comes further down, because active() sorts by group and then newest id. The project list is sorted by name, so with no project picked the page opens on the first name: r-projects.png shows api, with nothing to do, while webapp holds the orange dot. Tasks sit after every goal, including set-aside ones, so a task that needs you can be far below the fold. With many projects the owner has to scan every row at every check.
findings.principle: Primary task and visual hierarchy: what matters most comes first [SCR-2] [NNG-VH]; frequent need in view [SEC-8]; status visible [NNG-H1]. status.rs St::rank already defines this order and loose() already uses it.
findings.fix: In active(), sort by (group_rank, pill.0.rank(), newest id), so within Active it runs Needs you, Failed, Working, In review, then the rest. In list(), sort open rows by needs first, then running, then name; selected() then opens on the project that needs attention with no other change. Render the Tasks card above Active when any loose row is St::Needs. Update the tests active_goals_list_started_first_with_their_status, the_list_puts_projects_without_open_goals_last and the_picked_project_falls_back_to_the_first.

findings.title: A Needs you pill does not say what is needed, and offers nothing to do about it
findings.element: Projects › Active › goal row and its opened tasks, e.g. G3 Checkout on mobile and G4 Nightly export (r-projects-open.png)
findings.problem: G3 says Needs you, but opening it shows Done, Done, Queued, Queued: no task needs you and nothing explains why. The reason is in the goal's stopped field, which pill() reads and never shows; the sidebar says 'stopped for you' and the Goals page has Continue. Here the owner has to find the small G3 ref and go to the goal page. A task's question appears only after opening the goal. The sidebar's Needs you count reads 1 while this page shows at least 3 Needs you pills, which may partly be the seed.
findings.principle: Walkthrough Q2-Q4: the action must be noticed and tied to the result [NNG-CW]; recognition over recall [NNG-H6]; visibility of status [NNG-H1].
findings.fix: Add a reason field to GoalLine and draw it as a 12px line under the name in the warn colour: the stopped text (e.g. 'Wave 1 is done. Review it, then continue'), else the first St::Needs task's row line. Reuse goals_page's Action::Continue button on stopped goals, which is a one-click signal the owner's rules allow. Keep the pill as it is.

findings.title: The project list's status can contradict the goals it summarises
findings.element: Projects › project list › row (r-projects-api.png, r-projects-open.png)
findings.problem: Three separate faults. (1) api reads '1 goal · queued' while its only goal says Working with a blue bar: running counts sessions, and queued wins when none is found, so the absence of a session may be a seed effect, but the row can show this whenever the two sources differ. (2) The dot uses g.needs only, while the goal pill also fires on stopped, so a project whose only attention item is a stopped goal shows no dot, even though its goal says Needs you. (3) Needs you is shown only by an 8px dot: sub() has no words for it, and warn against accent is a colour-only difference.
findings.principle: Use of colour [WCAG 1.4.1]; one fact must not disagree with itself [SEC-7]; system status [NNG-H1].
findings.fix: Build the row's status from the same facts as the pill: needs |= i(g,"needs") > 0 || opt_s(g,"stopped").is_some(); count working from the goals' active minus needs as well as sessions. Put the count first in sub(), in words and the warn colour: '12 goals · 3 need you · 1 running'. Keep the dot as a second signal.

findings.title: Goal and task rows lose their name and status at narrow widths and under the task panel
findings.element: Projects › Active, Tasks and Finished rows at the 900x560 minimum window, and with the task panel open at 1360 wide
findings.problem: Computed from code, not seen in a capture. At 900 wide the fixed columns (sidebar 248, list 280) leave a card of about 306px. A goal row's fixed parts need 388px, so the name column shrinks to 0 and the card's overflow_hidden cuts the pill to about 30px. A task row needs 448px, so its title goes to 0 and its chip is clipped away. Goal names vanish below about 982 wide and task titles below about 1042. Separately, the 480px task panel floats over the page's right edge, so at 1360 it covers the bars and pills from x=880, and scrolling can't reveal them. The list has no planned collapse.
findings.principle: Layout reflows across the window range [HIG-MACOS]; the order holds as it narrows [SCR-6]; every feature reachable at every size [NNG-H6].
findings.fix: Choose from the width left for the main pane, with the task panel's 480 subtracted when it is open. Under 640: hide the 150px bar and keep the 'n of m' text. Under 520: drop the 190px meta column and put meta under the title. Under 460: replace the 280px list with a project pop-up menu above the header, which follows L2 for a set that grows. The pill and name stay visible at every width.

findings.title: The page cannot be used from the keyboard
findings.element: Projects › every control: project rows, Nothing open toggle, goal rows, refs, task links, Backlog, release and Show all links
findings.problem: Every control is a div with on_click. projects.rs has no track_focus, key handler or focus style, and the app source has no tab_index or accessibility calls at all. A Mac keyboard user can reach the page with a shortcut, but can't pick a project, open a goal or open a task, and no focus is shown. Assistive tech gets no names or roles. Rated 3 rather than 4 because the owner also has a pointer and the gap is app-wide. Backlog already has page focus and on_key.
findings.principle: Keyboard [WCAG 2.1.1]; focus visible [WCAG 2.4.7]; name, role, value [WCAG 4.1.2]; arrows move inside groups [MS-KBD].
findings.fix: Follow backlog.rs: give the page a focus handle and on_key. Up and Down move through project rows and then goal and task rows, Left and Right fold or open a goal, Enter opens a task or goal page, and F6 or Tab moves between the list and the main pane. Draw a 2px accent ring on the current row. Screen reader roles depend on what gpui_kit can expose, so that part may need separate work.

findings.title: On a paused goal, Start silently resumes everything, and the two Resumes differ
findings.element: Goal page › header and Paused banner, paused goal with planned tasks (g2-paused.png), 1360x860 dark
findings.problem: The banner says 'Nothing new starts', yet a blue 'Start 1 more task' sits above a blue 'Resume the goal'. The Start button posts to goals/G/run, and api.rs run_goal (lines 2853-2854) clears paused. So one click meant to add T11 also releases T9 and T10, and the toast only says 'Started: 1 task queued'. With no planned tasks the header shows 'Resume' (goal-run, which also runs resume_parked) beside the banner's 'Resume the goal' (a plain paused:false). The same word therefore does different things.
findings.principle: Visibility of status and consistency: one action, one name, one result, and one primary action per screen [NNG-H1] [NNG-H4] [NNG-H8] [SEC-5]
findings.fix: While paused, the banner holds the only Resume. In run_buttons_view, drop the header's goal-run button when paused, unless the start_failed case applies. Make the banner button call goal-run so parked tasks come back too, and label it 'Resume the goal', or 'Resume and start 1 more task' when planned > 0. Have run_toast say so: 'Going again: 1 task queued'.

findings.title: Pausing removes the goal from the sidebar while its tasks are still running
findings.element: Sidebar › Active goals and Goals count, after Pause (g2-paused.png against goal-g2.png)
findings.problem: On Pause, G2 disappears from the list and the Goals count drops from 2 to 1, while T8 and T2 still show Working. goal_group returns Paused before Active, and active_goals keeps only Active. A paused goal is the kind most likely to be forgotten, and the surface checked through the day stops showing it. The 'Paused · 2 of 7' branch in goal_sub can't be reached from this list.
findings.principle: Visibility of system status; recognition rather than recall [NNG-H1] [NNG-H6]
findings.fix: Render sidebar::pinned_goals filtered to Active and Paused, with paused goals after active ones so the existing 'Paused · 2 of 7' line shows, and count them in the Goals number. At the least, keep a paused goal listed while it has working or needs tasks. The source comment says this exclusion is deliberate, but no listed owner rule forbids the change.

findings.title: Resume confirms with a stale 'Paused' toast and a note that never clears
findings.element: Goal page › below the status bar, after Resume (g2-resumed.png)
findings.problem: After Resume the screen shows green 'Going again' and the toast 'Paused. Running tasks carry on.' at the same time, so the owner gets two opposite statuses. Resume writes only to the inline ggate note, so nothing replaces the toast. The note also pushes every card down 40px and stays. Only a later Resume or Bring it back clears it (goal.rs:812), reset_for leaves it, and Pause sends no group. It therefore comes back on reopening the goal, and a second Pause shows 'Going again' inside the PAUSED banner (gate() renders the note there).
findings.principle: Visibility of system status: the status shown must be true [NNG-H1]
findings.fix: In set_paused, pass grp = None for both directions, so Resume shows a 3s 'Going again' toast that replaces the Paused toast and the layout stays put. Failures then go to the 6s error toast. Do the same for bring_back, or clear ggate:{gr} when the banner state changes.

findings.title: Start, Pause, Resume and their menus can't be reached from the keyboard
findings.element: Goal page › header buttons, caret, Start menu rows, Start at, banner button; whole flow
findings.problem: kit::btn and the menu rows are plain divs with on_click, and taskboard-app/src contains no tab_index or tab_stop at all. No key binding starts, pauses or resumes a goal (app.rs:1577-1589). Only the Start at field takes focus, because the code focuses it. Pointer is the only route through the primary flow.
findings.principle: Keyboard operable, and every command reachable from a menu with its shortcut shown [WCAG 2.1.1] [MS-KBD] [HIG-MACOS]
findings.fix: Add .track_focus and .tab_index to kit::btn and btn_primary, with Enter and Space activating and a visible focus ring. Give menus Up, Down, Enter and Esc handling. Add a Goal menu to the menu bar with Start, Pause and Resume bound to shortcuts, for example Cmd+Return for Start and Cmd+Shift+P for Pause or Resume. The gap is app-wide, so fix it in the kit.

findings.title: A failed wave has no Needs you row, no release on its Goals row, and reads like a review stop in the sidebar
findings.element: Needs you; Goals › G4 row; Sidebar › G4, at 1360×860 and 1360×1240, dark, failed task
findings.problem: G4 is stopped by T54, but Needs you has no row for it (r-needs.png). The code explains why: `stage_entry` only uses `stopped_wave` (state 'stopped'), `stop_vm` filters on ' is done', and `on_fail`/`finish_task` raise no alert. The Goals row is red but offers Pause rather than a release (r-goals.png), because `goal_row` only sets Action::Continue for state 'stopped'. The sidebar gives G3 and G4 the same 'stopped for you', so a failure can't be told from a routine review. The owner must open the goal page to release it.
findings.principle: Consistency and standards [NNG-H4]; Recognition rather than recall [NNG-H6]; Visibility of system status [NNG-H1]
findings.fix: Emit a stage for the first unpassed wave in state 'failed' (`stage:G4:1`). In `stop_vm`, build 'Nightly export · T54 failed' with 'Holds 1 task', linked to T54 and kept in Decide (a kind other than 'Failed', which `kind_of` sends to Stopped). On the Goals row, add an action that opens the gate's choices, and don't leave Pause as the only signal. In `goal_sub`, branch on the line: 'T54 failed' for a failure, 'wave 1 ready for review' for a review stop.

findings.title: The Needs you badge reads 1, or nothing, while goals stand still
findings.element: Sidebar › nav › Needs you and Goals, all pages
findings.problem: The badge is `counts.waiting`, which is agents only. In r-needs.png it reads 1 while Decide holds 3 items and G4 and G5 are stopped too. `(needs > 0).then(...)` removes the number at 0, so after answering one question the nav shows no count and no sign that a goal waits at a stop. The count is accurate for agents, and 'Agents waiting' is honest wording. The result is that the app's one always-visible signal says nothing about stopped goals, and the owner glances at it through the day.
findings.principle: Visibility of system status [NNG-H1]; squint test, the attention signal should match what needs attention [SCR-2]
findings.fix: Keep the agents-only number. Add a second, quieter signal on the Goals nav item: '8' plus an 8px `t.warn` dot, or '3 stopped' in muted text, when any active goal has a `stopped` line or a held wave. Also draw a plain muted dot on Needs you when Decide has items and the agent count is 0. Neither changes the count rule; changing the number itself would need the owner's OK.

findings.title: The failed gate's main action skips the failure, and Try again is out of sight
findings.element: Goal page › Wave 1 › gate, r-g4.png, 1360×860, dark, failed task
findings.problem: 'T54 failed. Wave 2 waits.' offers one blue button: 'Continue anyway'. The daemon's own hold reason says 'Try again, or continue past it', but Try again exists only inside T54's task panel (`done_node`); the row's `retry` covers start failures only. The reason is cut to 'The bucket refused the uplo…', so the owner decides without it. One click runs wave 2 on top of a failed upload, and nothing on this page undoes it.
findings.principle: Error prevention [NNG-H5]; Help users recover from errors [NNG-H9]; destructive or risky actions are separated from safe ones [NNG-H3]
findings.fix: In `gate()` for the failed case, put the reason in the text: 'T54 failed: the bucket refused the upload. Wave 2 waits.' Add 'Try T54 again' as the btn_primary, calling `POST tasks/T54/requeue`, as the panel's Try again does. Make 'Continue anyway' a plain secondary button. With several failures, use 'Try 2 again'. Both are one-click signals, so no owner rule changes.

findings.title: Gate buttons appear to have no keyboard route
findings.element: Goal page › gate button; Goals › row Continue; Needs you › Continue
findings.problem: `btn_primary` and `btn_small` are plain clickable divs, and kit.rs has no `track_focus` or `tab_index` anywhere, so Tab can't appear to reach Continue or 'Let wave 2 start'. The releases seem to be mouse-only on a pointer-and-keyboard platform. I read this from code and did not press keys, and an app-level shortcut could still exist.
findings.principle: Keyboard [WCAG 2.1.1]; Focus visible [WCAG 2.4.7]; Tab reaches controls [MS-KBD]
findings.fix: Give kit's `btn_base` a focus handle or `tab_index(0)`, a visible 2px focus ring in `t.accent`, and Enter and Space activation. Then every gate, row and Needs you button gets it at once. Confirm in the running app by tabbing to 'Continue to wave 2' and pressing Space.

findings.title: Pause can't be undone in place, and paused goals go quiet
findings.element: Goals › row Pause and Paused shelf (goals-both-paused.png)
findings.problem: One click on a 24px button moves the goal out of the list to a shelf. The toast 'Paused. Running tasks carry on.' has no Undo, and the shelf line has no Resume: the owner must open the goal page and use its banner. The shelf shows only 'Paused · 1 of 4', although G1 had a worker running and an open question. The sidebar's Needs you count also goes from 1 (goals.png) to blank; whether that's intended wasn't checked.
findings.principle: User control and freedom [NNG-H3]; Visibility of system status [NNG-H1]
findings.fix: Add Undo to the toast, calling set_paused(false). Add a small Resume button to each Paused shelf line, which is a one-click signal the owner rules allow. Replace the filler 'Paused · ' prefix, since the shelf title already says it, with live state: '1 of 4 · 1 working · 1 needs you'.

findings.title: The shelf strip never wraps, so narrow tiles lose goal names
findings.element: Goals › Up next, Paused, Set aside, Finished this week at 900x560
findings.problem: shelf_strip is one no-wrap row of equal columns, and each line's meta is flex_none. At 900 wide there's about 596px of content, so three shelves leave about 159px inside a tile and four leave about 108px. '2 PRs merged · 6:24 PM' alone is about 127px, leaving no room for the name. Inferred from code and measured widths: no capture shows shelves at this size, or the four-shelf layout.
findings.principle: Every control at every size [SCR-6]; Recognition rather than recall [NNG-H6]
findings.fix: Use flex-wrap with a 280px minimum column, so shelves fall to two columns or one. Under about 240px of tile width, put meta on its own line under the name.

findings.title: Section counts fail text contrast in both themes
findings.element: Goals › group labels' counts: In progress 8, Up next 4, and so on (r-goals.png, r-goals-light.png)
findings.problem: group_label draws the count in t.faint at 12px on the page background: 2.84:1 in light (#8a95a3 on #f6f7f9) and 4.31:1 in dark (#6f7a88 on #0f1216). Both are under 4.5:1.
findings.principle: Contrast [WCAG 1.4.3]
findings.fix: Use t.muted for the count: #5f6b7a gives 5.06:1 on the light background. Keep the weight difference from the title.

findings.title: Progress bar segments can't be told apart
findings.element: Goals › row progress bar (r-goals-light.png, r-goals.png)
findings.problem: Queued, Planned and Stopped all use t.border_2, at 1.48:1 on the light card and 1.63:1 on the dark card, so unstarted work barely shows and a stopped task looks queued. Needs and Failed differ by hue only: 1.27:1 against each other in light and 1.35:1 in dark. Segments have no label or tooltip. The status text carries the headline, but the bar's breakdown can't be read.
findings.principle: Non-text contrast [WCAG 1.4.11]; Use of colour [WCAG 1.4.1]
findings.fix: Fill Queued and Planned with t.faint: 3.04:1 on the light card, about 3.8:1 on the dark card. Give Planned a hollow outline to separate it from Queued, and Stopped its own solid colour. Add a hover tooltip per segment ('2 queued'). Put Failed and Needs apart in parts(), or raise the lightness gap between them.

findings.title: G4 reads 'failed' on the page and 'stopped for you' in the sidebar
findings.element: Goals › G4 Nightly export row against sidebar line (r-goals.png)
findings.problem: The row says '1 failed', driven by wave state. sidebar.rs says '1 of 3 · stopped for you', driven by the goal's stopped field, and goal_row's summary fallback says 'Stopped for your review' until details land. So G4's state changes by place and time, there's no Continue, and the owner can't tell whether to review or to fix. G3 shows the same 'stopped for you' wording with a real Continue.
findings.principle: One fact, one place [SEC-7]; Consistency [NNG-H4]
findings.fix: Decide the goal's state once and share it. If a wave failed, say '1 failed' in the row, the sidebar and the summary fallback. Use 'stopped for you' only when a Continue exists.

findings.title: Folded 'Queued' doesn't say what it's waiting for, and 'press Start' has no Start
findings.element: Goals › G5, G6 folded rows; open task rows T51, T52, T79 (r-goals.png, r-goals-open.png, r-goals-expand-all.png)
findings.problem: G5 reads only 'Queued', with no second line. next_line never uses the task's waiting text, so a goal held by hours, a wave or the owner looks the same. The 'Waits for you to press Start' wording here is a seed effect: waits_for_start only returns true for pickup=manual, so it isn't rated as a bug. The gap behind it is real: task_row has actions only for Needs and Review, so a manual task says press Start with no Start in the row, and the folded row hides that it waits on you.
findings.principle: Visibility of system status [NNG-H1]; Walkthrough Q2 [NNG-CW]
findings.fix: When a goal has nothing running, let next_line fall back to the first queued task's waiting line. If that task waits for Start, add a Start button in task_row's action slot, a one-click signal the rules allow, and rank the goal with those needing the owner.

findings.title: Finished shelf keeps its 'this week' title when showing older goals
findings.element: Goals › Finished this week › 'N earlier' link
findings.problem: Expanding earlier adds older goals to the same tile under 'Finished this week', and the count stays at this week's number. With nothing finished this week the shelf reads 'FINISHED THIS WEEK 0' with only a link in it. No capture shows this; it is read from shelf_tile and shelf_strip.
findings.principle: Match with the real world [NNG-H2]; Visibility of system status [NNG-H1]
findings.fix: With earlier on, title the shelf 'Finished' and count lines plus earlier, or add a quiet 'Earlier' sub-label above the older lines. With zero this week, title it 'Finished' and show the link alone.

findings.title: Project filter can disappear while still applied, and its counts don't match the page
findings.element: Goals › header › project filter (r-goals-filter-menu.png)
findings.problem: The control only renders when tabs.len() > 1, and tabs leave out finished goals. If 'api' is picked and the other project's open goals all finish, only one tab is left: the filter vanishes but stays applied, hiding the other project's finished goals with no way to clear it. Counts also leave out finished goals, so the menu's 'webapp 12' is likely one less than the 13 goals the page shows, if G10 is webapp.
findings.principle: User control and freedom [NNG-H3]; Readouts tell the truth [NNG-H1]
findings.fix: Render the filter when tabs.len() > 1 or project != "all". Count every goal the filter would show, finished this week included, or reset to 'all' when the control hides.

findings.title: A failed detail fetch shows 'Loading…' forever
findings.element: Goals › open row body
findings.problem: app.rs keeps goal_rows only on Ok and silently drops an Err. goal_body then shows 'Loading…' until a later refresh succeeds, the wave text stays blank, and the row falls back to summary counts. The owner can't tell slow from broken. Read from code; the state wasn't captured.
findings.principle: Help users recover from errors [NNG-H9]; each state designed [NNG-H1]
findings.fix: Record failed refs next to details. In goal_body, show 'Couldn't load this goal's tasks' with a Try again link that calls m.refresh. Clear the entry on land().

findings.title: Goal rows and shelves aren't virtualized
findings.element: Goals › In progress list, open bodies, shelf tiles, 'N earlier'
findings.problem: render() builds every card, every task of every open goal, and every shelf line in plain loops inside one scroller. The earlier list grows without end and an Up next tile has no cap. This breaks the owner's rule that long lists are virtualized, and Expand all is the worst case.
findings.principle: Owner rule: long lists virtualized; Aesthetic and minimalist design [NNG-H8]
findings.fix: Flatten the page into row items (group label, goal head, wave head, task row, shelf strip) and draw them with gpui's list(), as home/view.rs, review.rs and releases.rs do with their virtual lists. Cap each shelf at 8 lines with an 'N more' link.

findings.title: Tasks aren't indented under their wave header
findings.element: Goals › open row › wave headers and task rows (r-goals-open.png, r-goals-expand-all.png)
findings.problem: wave_head and task_row both start at INSET (60px): 'Wave 1 · Measure' and the 'Done' chip share a left edge. Only the band colour marks the group, and the owner has already corrected this pattern.
findings.principle: LESSONS L1: label above members, members indented under it; Grouped by space [SEC-2]
findings.fix: Set task_row's left padding to INSET + 16 (76px) when it sits under a wave or 'No wave' header. Keep 60px for goals with no waves, which have no header.

findings.title: The goal ref is a small target and the row gives no hover cue
findings.element: Goals › row › ref link and row head (r-goals.png)
findings.problem: The ref is the row's only route to the goal page. It is bare 12px text, about 14–21 wide and 17 high, under the 24px floor, and it sits inside a clickable row, so a near miss expands the row. goal_head has a pointer cursor but no hover style, unlike task_row, and the 12px chevron is the only hint that it opens.
findings.principle: Target size [WCAG 2.5.8]; Frequent targets [NNG-FITTS]; States [NNG-H1]
findings.fix: Give the ref min 24x24 with padding and a matching negative margin so the layout doesn't move. Add .hover(bg t.panel_2) to goal_head, as task_row has, and enlarge the chevron to 14px.

findings.title: Expand all and Collapse all don't track state or scope
findings.element: Goals › header › Expand all, Collapse all (r-goals-filtered.png, r-goals-expand-all.png)
findings.problem: Both show at all times, even for one row (r-goals-filtered.png) and even when they would do nothing. Expand all opens only the filtered goals, but Collapse all clears m.goals.open, including rows open under another project, so switching the filter back finds them shut.
findings.principle: Consistency [NNG-H4]; Everything earns its place [SCR-5]
findings.fix: Use one button that reads 'Collapse all' when any shown row is open and 'Expand all' when none is, hidden when going.len() == 1. Make it remove only the refs in going.

findings.title: 'Side by side' contradicts the waves on the same screen
findings.element: How it runs › Order, goal-g2.png and g2-large.png
findings.problem: Order says 'Side by side', while wave 3 reads 'After wave 2' and T10 reads 'Waits for wave 2 to start T9'. how_runs maps run_in_order false to 'Side by side' even when waves exist, but runner.rs holds tasks by wave regardless ('Waves take the place of running in order'). The owner can't trust the panel that explains how the goal runs.
findings.principle: One fact, one place [SEC-7]; consistency [NNG-H4]
findings.fix: Change the match in how_runs so any waved goal reads 'By wave'; 'In order, by wave' only adds noise. Keep 'In order' and 'Side by side' for goals without waves.

findings.title: Two time formats on one page, one against the owner's AM/PM rule
findings.element: Header scheduled button r-g12.png ('Starts tomorrow at 1:55am'); sidebar in r-g3-hours.png ('Agents off until Sat 3am'); tooltips, menus and toasts via fmt::clock12
findings.problem: Run signals use lowercase '1:55am' while task rows and wave headers use '6:25 PM'. The owner's rule is 12-hour times with AM/PM, and the doc comment on scheduled_at even promises 'today at 5 PM'. clock12 is the source, so every run message has the mismatch.
findings.principle: Owner rule: 12-hour times with AM/PM; consistency [NNG-H4]
findings.fix: Make clock12 return '1:55 AM' and '3 PM', with a space and capitals, and update its tests and doc comment. Check callers such as the sidebar work hours chip for width. The Start at field's placeholder '5pm, tomorrow 9am' can stay, as it's an input hint.

findings.title: Outside work hours, Pause is hidden and the time is cut off
findings.element: Goal page › header and wave rows, r-g3-hours.png
findings.problem: Pause vanishes from the header when the split button and waiting state coincide (line 333, !(split && waiting)). It moves into the caret menu, whose tooltip only says 'Start now or at a set time instead'. 'Start tomorrow: 1 more task' also reads as if the goal is idle until tomorrow, while T8 is Working and wave 2 says Now. The row reason is cut to 'Waits for work hours (tomorr…', losing the time, and the page says 'tomorrow' while the sidebar says 'Sat'.
findings.principle: Recognition rather than recall [NNG-H6]; frequent in view [SEC-8]
findings.fix: When split && waiting, still push the plain Pause button instead of hiding it, and remove Pause from start_menu_view. Or, at minimum, change the caret tooltip to 'Start now, at a set time, or pause'. State the hours once on the goal, for example a line under the progress bar, 'Queued tasks start tomorrow at 3 AM', and shorten the row reason to 'Work hours' so it fits.

findings.title: A missed outcome reads as finished and has no next step
findings.element: Goal page › progress line, r-g13.png
findings.problem: The bar is full green and the only signal is right-aligned amber text. Every other stopped state gets a banner or gate, but this one has none, and the only button is Open in Claude. 'Outcome not met · 2 misses' is plain text that opens a menu with no affordance beyond hover, and that menu repeats the Backlog list in the aside.
findings.principle: Visibility of system status [NNG-H1]; looks like what it is [SEC-4]; one fact, one place [SEC-7]
findings.fix: Extend gate_view with a third banner: label 'Outcome not met', text 'Every task is done, but 2 misses hold this goal open.', with the two misses linked. Drop the click menu from the progress line, since the Backlog section already opens each issue. Add a trailing warn segment to the bar so it no longer reads as complete.

findings.title: A goal with no tasks has no empty state
findings.element: Goal page › main column, r-g11.png
findings.problem: The header shows an empty bar and '0 of 0 done', then the left column is blank beside a How it runs panel for work that doesn't exist. goal_state already has 'No tasks yet', but it never reaches the screen. Nothing says what to do next, and Open in Claude isn't presented as that step.
findings.principle: Empty states with a way forward [mobile:NNG-EMPTY]; help users know what's next [NNG-H1]
findings.fix: When there are no tasks, replace the bar and count with 'No tasks yet', and fill the main column with one line: 'This goal has no plan yet. Open it in Claude to add tasks.' Make Open in Claude the primary button in this state only. Hide the Terminals row while there is nothing to run.

findings.title: 'Resume' appears on a goal that isn't paused, and Pause goes away
findings.element: Goal page › header buttons, state with a task whose start failed (goal.rs lines 310-333); no capture
findings.problem: With a start_failed task and nothing planned, the label falls through to 'Resume' on a goal that was never paused, while the tooltip talks about tasks that couldn't start. The !unstarted guard also removes Pause, so one failed start leaves no way to pause the rest of the goal. A goal with a lost task, which goal_state calls 'Needs a restart', gets only Pause in the header, though goal-level Restart exists on Home.
findings.principle: Match between the system and the real world [NNG-H2]; user control and freedom [NNG-H3]
findings.fix: For unstarted, label the button 'Try again' (or 'Try 2 again'), and drop !unstarted from the Pause condition. For lost tasks, show 'Restart' on the goal header using the same goals/:g/restart signal as Home.

findings.title: 'Waits for you to press Start' can appear with no Start on the goal
findings.element: Goal page › queued rows and header, r-g3.png, r-g4.png, r-g5.png
findings.problem: On these three captures the line is a seed effect: waits_for_start needs manual pickup in a goal with no ran_at, which a goal that really ran doesn't have, so don't read those pages as the live text. The gap behind it is real. Agents add queued tasks with manual pickup (reports.rs line 2965). In a never-run goal with nothing planned, run_buttons_view shows no Start, only Pause, because the run branch needs planned > 0 or a paused or unstarted goal. goals/:g/run would resume these tasks, but nothing offers it. The task panel has its own Start, though I didn't trace whether it shows in this state.
findings.principle: Walkthrough question 2, will users notice the correct action [NNG-CW]; consistency [NNG-H4]
findings.fix: Add a parked count to run_buttons_view (status queued, pickup manual, no line_session, goal not run). When it's above 0, show the primary 'Start' with the title 'Queue the tasks waiting for Start'. This needs pickup and ran_at in the goal payload if they aren't already there.

findings.title: 'Wave 2 is held.' doesn't say why or until when
findings.element: Goal page › Wave 2 gate, r-g5.png
findings.problem: The review stop gate explains itself ('Look it over, then let wave 2 start'), but the held gate only restates the header's 'Held'. The owner can't tell who held it, whether anything else will release it, or whether it's safe to let go. The backend's wording is more useful ('is held until it's continued') but doesn't reach this gate.
findings.principle: Visibility of system status [NNG-H1]; no filler labels (owner rule)
findings.fix: Change the gate text to 'Wave 2 won't start until you let it.' If the hold has a recorded reason or author, append it, for example 'Held by Claude: waiting on the API change'. Keep the 'Let wave 2 start' button.

findings.title: The Start caret opens a one-item menu that opens another popover
findings.element: Goal › header › Start caret › Start menu, inside work hours (g2-start-menu.png, r-g7-start-menu.png)
findings.problem: Outside the after-hours case, start_menu_items returns only 'Start at…', so the menu is a single row that must be clicked to reach the real field. That is one extra click and a jump to a new place on screen, with a tooltip saying the same thing as the row.
findings.principle: Flexibility and efficiency; every element earns its place [NNG-H7] [NNG-H8] [SCR-5]
findings.fix: When start_menu_items returns one item, have the caret call open_at_menu directly. Keep the sentence 'It starts then, whatever the work hours' as help text in the popover (see R60). Keep the menu for the after-hours case, where it has two or three real choices.

findings.title: Menus open at the pointer, not under their button
findings.element: Goal › header › all menus, 1360x860 (g2-start-menu.png, g2-start-at.png, r-g12-menu.png, r-g13-misses.png)
findings.problem: Every menu opens at click x minus 240 (minus 300 for misses), so where it lands depends on where on the button you clicked, and on a wide button that can shift it a long way. The menus don't line up with their triggers and they cover nearby facts: the '2 of 7 done' readout, and the How it runs heading and task time in r-g13-misses.png. Start at jumps again, to below the row that was clicked, about 390px left of the caret, with nothing connecting it to Start. kit::popover's own comment says it is 'anchored under the element that opened it', which isn't what happens.
findings.principle: Consistency; menus sit next to what opened them [NNG-H4] [desktop:HIG-POINTER]
findings.fix: Anchor each menu to its trigger's bounds: right edge flush with the button's right edge, 6px below it. Capture the bounds with on_prepaint or a canvas measure rather than e.position(). Open Start at in the same anchor as the menu it replaces, so it swaps in place. Align the misses menu's right edge with the end of 'Outcome not met'.

findings.title: 'Cancel' in the scheduled menu reads as close, but drops the schedule at once
findings.element: Goal › header › scheduled menu › Cancel (r-g12-menu.png)
findings.problem: In a menu, 'Cancel' usually means 'never mind'. Here it removes the scheduled start immediately, with no confirm and no Undo, and the time has to be retyped to get it back. It is the last row, right where someone looking to dismiss would click.
findings.principle: User control and freedom; destructive actions are worded clearly and can be undone [NNG-H3] [NNG-H5]
findings.fix: Rename the row 'Remove start time', with the sub 'It stays planned until you press Start'. Separate it from the two rows above with a divider. Use m.toast_undo for 'G12 isn't scheduled any more', with an Undo that posts the previous start_at back to goals/{gr}/run.

findings.title: The Start at field has no label, loses its format hint and has a faint edge
findings.element: Goal › Start at popover (g2-start-at.png)
findings.problem: The only guidance is the placeholder '5pm, tomorrow 9am', which goes away as soon as you type. The 'whatever the work hours' note stayed behind in the menu. In Change the time the field opens empty, so the current time isn't shown and the button still says 'Start at'. The field border #3a424d on #1a1f26 is about 1.6:1 (#cfd5dd on white about 1.5:1), and the field fill matches the popover. The caret also sits on the placeholder's first character, so '5pm' is hard to read.
findings.principle: Visible labels; formats stated before typing; 3:1 for control boundaries [WCAG 3.3.2] [WCAG 1.4.11] [NNG-H5] [mobile:NNG-PLACEHOLDER]
findings.fix: Add a 12px label above the field, 'Start at', and a help line below it, 'Like 5pm or tomorrow 9am. It starts then, whatever the work hours.' Rename the button to 'Schedule', since the label now carries 'Start at'. From Change the time, prefill the field with the current time, select it, and label the button 'Change'. Use a border colour with at least 3:1 against the card, such as #6f7a88 (t.faint) on dark, plus an accent border on focus. Put 2px of padding before the placeholder.

findings.title: Scheduled and waiting times break the AM/PM rule and read three ways
findings.element: Goal › header › scheduled button, waiting button and their tooltips, toasts (r-g12-menu.png, r-g6-hours-menu.png)
findings.problem: The header shows 'Starts tomorrow at 1:55am', 'Waiting until tomorrow 3am' and '(tomorrow at 3am)', while the same screen shows 'Done 6:25 PM'. The sidebar pill gives the same moment as 'Sat 3am'. The owner's rule is 12-hour times with AM/PM. fmt::clock12 returns lowercase with no space, although the comment on scheduled_at promises 'today at 5 PM'.
findings.principle: Consistency: same thing, same form [NNG-H4]; owner rule on 12-hour times with AM/PM
findings.fix: Change fmt::clock12 to return '1:55 AM' and '3 PM', and update its tests at fmt.rs:376-378 and any strings that rely on it, including the hours pill. Check the daemon's hours::say_when for the same format. Use one pattern in the button labels: 'Starts tomorrow at 1:55 AM' and 'Waiting until tomorrow at 3 AM'.

findings.title: A start more than a week away shows only a weekday
findings.element: Goal › header › scheduled button and its toast (scheduled_at, goal.rs:240)
findings.problem: parse_at accepts a full date such as 2026-11-20T09:00, but scheduled_at prints any date past tomorrow with %A. A start two weeks out reads 'Starts Friday at 9am', which looks like this week's Friday, so the owner could believe work starts sooner than it will. opens_at has the same pattern. Seen in code only, with no capture of this state.
findings.principle: Visibility of system status; readouts tell the truth [NNG-H1]
findings.fix: Use the weekday only within the next 6 days. Beyond that, use 'Nov 20 at 9 AM'. Share one helper between scheduled_at and opens_at, since they repeat the same day logic.

findings.title: 'Outcome not met' doesn't look clickable
findings.element: Goal › header › progress readout › Outcome not met (r-g13-misses.png)
findings.problem: It renders as coloured status text beside the count, and the underline appears only on hover, so nothing says it opens a menu. Every other menu trigger in this header has a ▾. The menu then repeats the same rows as the Backlog section right below it, with the same issues shown twice on screen and the menu covering the top of that aside.
findings.principle: Looks like what it is; one fact, one place [WCAG 1.4.11] [NNG-H6] [SEC-4] [SEC-7]
findings.fix: Add a ▾ after the text and a permanent underline, matching the other triggers. Keep the menu, because the Backlog section shows only the first few issues, and anchor it under the trigger as in R58.

findings.title: The misses menu has no height limit
findings.element: Goal › misses menu (misses_menu, goal view lines 209-236)
findings.problem: Every open miss becomes a row in a plain div, with no max height, scrolling or virtualizing. A goal with many misses gets a menu taller than the window; it snaps to the window and the rows past the edge can't be reached. Titles also truncate with no tooltip. Only two rows were captured; the overflow comes from reading the code.
findings.principle: Owner rule: long lists virtualized; every item reachable [NNG-H6]
findings.fix: Cap the menu at min(360px, window height minus 80px) and render rows through the app's virtual list, as the goal page's lists do. Add a tooltip with the full title on truncated rows.

findings.title: Crumbs and the ref row say the same thing back to back
findings.element: Goal › crumbs and header ref row, all captures
findings.problem: 'Goals › webapp › G2' is followed 40px lower by 'G2 [webapp]'. Both the project crumb and the project pill go to the same place, so two rows of chrome carry one fact and sit above the title.
findings.principle: One fact, one place; everything earns its place [SEC-7] [SCR-5]
findings.fix: Remove the ref row's G2 and project pill and keep the crumbs. Make the crumb's G2 selectable (sel 'goal-ref'), move the repo_path tooltip to the project crumb, and put the epic link at the end of the crumb row. This also returns about 28px to the pinned header.

findings.title: A long goal name makes the pinned header eat the page
findings.element: Goal › header › title, long name G6 (r-g6.png, r-g6-hours-menu.png), projected to 900x560
findings.problem: The title has no line limit and the header doesn't scroll. The 86-character name takes two lines at 1360 (confirmed). At 900 wide, with the buttons beside it, the title has about 330px and would take about five lines. Added to a tldr and a gate banner, that would leave little of the 560px height for the waves.
findings.principle: Sticky areas leave room for content [WCAG 1.4.10] [SCR-1]
findings.fix: Clamp the title to two lines with line_clamp(2) and show the full name in a tooltip. When the window height is under about 640, let the tldr scroll with the body rather than stay pinned.

findings.title: The open task isn't marked, and the panel cuts the page off
findings.element: Goal page › task rows with the right panel open, 1360×860 (g2-task-panel.png)
findings.problem: With T8 open, its row looks like every other row, because row_el takes no selected state. After a look at the panel, the owner has to read the ref in the panel to find their place. The 480px panel floats over the page without reflow, so it cuts 'Review stop a…', hides status lines, PR and age columns, and covers the whole aside.
findings.principle: Selected row marked [NNG-H1]; selection shown in each pane [tablet:AND-CANON]
findings.fix: Pass the open ref into row_el and draw that row with t.accent_soft and a 2px t.accent left edge. Keep the one home in the right panel. When the panel is open, add 480px of right padding to lists::body and hide the aside, so cards reflow rather than being cut, using R20's column-hiding steps.

findings.title: Waiting words don't say what is actually holding the work
findings.element: Goal page › wave header meta and queued rows (r-g6.png wave 3, goal-g2.png T9 and T10)
findings.problem: Three cases. In r-g6.png wave 3 says 'After wave 2' although wave 2 is done, because head() ignores the previous wave's state. In goal-g2.png, T10's 'Waits for wave 2 to start T9' reads as if wave 2 is a thing that starts T9, and it repeats the header's 'After wave 2'. T9 is Queued with a blank line although 'How it runs' shows 3 at most and 1 in use, because status::row drops tile_vm's fallback line for queued tasks. The owner can't tell waiting from stuck.
findings.principle: Visibility of system status [NNG-H1]; match with the real world [NNG-H2]; will users see progress [NNG-CW]
findings.fix: In head(), when the previous wave is done or passed, show 'Next' (or the task line's reason) rather than 'After wave N'. In daemon hold_reason, change the text to 'Waits for T9 to start'. In status::row, use tile.line for Queued instead of an empty string, and check its 'When a terminal is free' fallback is true when terminals are free.

findings.title: A human task's row doesn't say what the owner must do
findings.element: Goal page › task row H49 and related counts, sample board (g1-needs.png)
