findings.problem: H49 is a task for the owner, yet its loud orange line is 'Updated just now', which comes from tile_vm's generic since('Updated'), and its PR cell says 'Ships one PR', because pr_cell doesn't check the task kind. Beside it, 'How it runs' reads '2 at most · 3 in use', because how_runs counts every needs task as a terminal. The progress line says '2 needs you' (lower-cased label, no plural), while the sidebar under it says '2 need you' and the Needs you nav count shows 1. The nav mismatch's cause wasn't traced.
findings.principle: Match with the real world [NNG-H2]; one fact, one place [SEC-7]; readouts tell the truth [NNG-H1]; owner rule: no filler labels
findings.fix: For kind human, make the row line the action ('Do this yourself' plus the task's first line) and return an empty PR cell. In how_runs, count only tasks with a live terminal (terminal_open), leaving out human tasks. In progress(), use fmt::plural so it says '2 need you'. Check that the nav count and the goal agree.

findings.title: Plan review findings name tasks but can't open them
findings.element: Goal page › Plan review › finding rows, refs at right (g1-plan-review.png, g1-review-open.png)
findings.problem: 'T2', 'T3' and 'T2, G2' are one joined plain-text string. Clicking the row only folds the detail, and a finding with no detail ('Overlaps another goal') does nothing. The owner has to find the task by hand in the list below or in another goal.
findings.principle: Recognition rather than recall [NNG-H6]; flexibility and efficiency [NNG-H7]
findings.fix: Keep tasks and refs as a list in Finding and draw each with kit::link. A T or H ref calls m.open_task, a G ref opens the goal page, and cx.stop_propagation stops the row folding. This is navigation only, so the read-only rule holds.

findings.title: Plan review is louder than the question that needs an answer
findings.element: Goal page › Plan review section above the lists (g1-plan-review.png, g1-review-open.png)
findings.problem: All four kind labels are bold orange in the same family as 'Needs you', though only 'Needs the owner' asks for the owner. The section can't be folded and pushes the task list down about 167px, or about 218px with two findings open, so the page's most emphasised block is not the live T3 question. Kind labels vary in width, so the finding text starts at four different x positions. On a short window (560 minimum) a long review could leave the waves about 100px, which is computed, not seen.
findings.principle: One emphasis [SEC-5]; squint test [SCR-2]; the work dominates [SCR-1]; alignment [SCR-4]
findings.fix: Draw kind labels in t.muted and keep t.warn_text only for 'Needs the owner', sorted first. Give the kind a fixed 150px column so the text lines up. Add a fold to the section head, showing 'Plan review · 4 findings · 1 needs you', folded by default once seen for that review.

findings.title: A failed or running review looks the same as a clean one
findings.element: Goal page › Plan review section, review state not done (review.rs findings())
findings.problem: findings() returns nothing for running, skipped or failed reviews, and section() then draws nothing. The owner can't tell 'reviewed, no problems' from 'the review failed'. Starting a new review also makes the current findings disappear until it ends. This is written down as intended in the file header, but it isn't one of the owner's listed rules.
findings.principle: Visibility of system status [NNG-H1]; help users recognize errors [NNG-H9]
findings.fix: Draw one muted line in the section's place: 'Plan review running', 'Plan review failed 6:51 PM' or 'Plan review skipped'. Say nothing only for a clean or absent review. While a re-run is going, keep the last finished findings with 'Running again' at the right of the head. If the daemon only sends the latest row, it needs to send the previous findings too.

findings.title: 'From other goals' doesn't say which goal, and group dots imply a state
findings.element: Goal page › No wave and From other goals cards (goal-g2.png)
findings.problem: T2 sits under 'From other goals', but neither the header nor the row says it belongs to G1, and WRow has no goal field. The group label stops short of naming its members' owner, which is the confusion L1 records. Both group headers also carry the same grey dot as a queued wave, though they have no state. 'No wave' gives no hint when T11 runs.
findings.principle: Lesson L1 (label above members); consistent labels [SEC-6]; one look per role [SEC-4]
findings.fix: Group shared rows by source goal, with a header per goal such as 'G1 · Sign-in with passkeys' linking to the goal, and rows under it. If the shared cards don't carry the goal, add it in ops.rs. Make Head.dot optional and draw no dot on these two groups. Give No wave a meta only if it's a real fact, for example 'Not part of the wave order'.

findings.title: A failed wave's only offer is a primary 'Continue anyway'
findings.element: Goal page › wave card gate, failed wave (waves.rs gate(), gate_el())
findings.problem: From code only, no capture shows a gate. The daemon's own wording is 'Try again, or continue past it', but the gate offers just 'Continue anyway' in primary style, and rows offer Try again only for failed starts. The riskiest choice on the page looks like the recommended one, with no link to the failed task. 'T36 failed' is plain text. If a wave is ever failed with an empty failed list, the text reads ' failed. Wave 6 waits.', and whether that can happen wasn't traced.
findings.principle: Error recovery [NNG-H9]; error prevention [NNG-H5]; one primary action [NNG-H8]
findings.fix: Keep the one click, so no owner rule changes. Draw 'Continue anyway' with the secondary button style, make each failed ref a link that opens its task, and add the same retry signal the task panel uses if one exists for failed tasks. Fall back to 'A task failed.' when the list is empty.

findings.unit: Goal aside: Attached, Notes, Devices, Bits
findings.title: Attached: the wave picker's scope and the counts disagree
findings.element: Goal page › aside › Attached (goal-g2.png, g2-wave-menu.png, g2-att-kinds.png), 1360x860 dark
findings.problem: The picker says Wave 2, but the first group under it is GOAL, whose files belong to no wave. The numbers then don't match: the head says 4 of 7 and the kinds menu says All kinds 4, while the wave menu says Wave 2 2 and All waves 5, because the menu leaves out the goal's 2 files. Picking All waves gives 7, not the 5 the row promised. GOAL also uses the same 11px bold capitals as the ATTACHED section head, so it reads as a peer section, and its files aren't indented under it while T8's are.
findings.principle: One fact, one place [SEC-7]; visibility of system status [NNG-H1]; a group's label sits above its members and they indent under it [LESSONS L1]
findings.fix: In attached_piece, put the GOAL group directly under the head and the wave picker below it, so the picker only heads what it filters. Show the wave's count at the picker's right edge, matching the menu row, so the card reads GOAL 2 + Wave 2 2 = 4 of 7 (or 2 + 5 = 7 on All waves). Draw the Goal label like a task label (12px medium, t.text_2) and indent its files with pl(12) as task_group does.

findings.unit: Goal aside: Attached, Notes, Devices, Bits
findings.title: What needs the owner sits at the bottom of the aside, under static settings
findings.element: Goal page › aside › section order (g2-devices.png, r-g13.png, g1-notes.png)
findings.problem: The fixed order puts How it runs first and Bits and Backlog last, yet those two hold what stops a goal: Misses goal and Blocks goal pills, and Not created bits, which goal.rs says hold back a finished goal. In g2-devices.png, opening Devices pushes Bits to the fold at 860 tall, with its heading cut off. On r-g13.png the header says Outcome not met, and the two issues that explain it come after settings and Devices. This works against the primary task: see what needs attention.
findings.principle: Frequent in view, rare behind [SEC-8]; the most important content draws the eye first [SCR-2] [NNG-VH]
findings.fix: In lists.rs build(), order the aside by need: Backlog first when any open issue has misses_goal or blocks, and Bits next when any is Not created. Then Notes, Attached and Devices, with How it runs last. With nothing needing the owner, keep Backlog and Bits after Devices. Sort rows inside Bits the same way (R77).

findings.unit: Goal aside: Attached, Notes, Devices, Bits
findings.title: Bits: the count doesn't match the list, and a Not created bit has no way forward
findings.element: Goal page › aside › Bits (g1-notes.png), 1360x1100 dark
findings.problem: The head says 1 of 2 created above three rows, because the count skips local bits and nothing says so. The one row that needs the owner, passkeys.settings Not created, comes last. It also shows no action: the link appears only when [bits] create_url is set, and otherwise the row gives no next step, even though this state can hold a finished goal open.
findings.principle: Visibility of system status [NNG-H1]; help users recover [NNG-H9]; recognition rather than recall [NNG-H6]
findings.fix: Change the head to name what's left: 1 not created, with no count when none are waiting. Sort bit_rows with warn first, then up, then muted. When create is None on a Not created bit, add a muted 12px line with the exact tb bit command that marks it made. This stays read-only.

findings.unit: Goal aside: Attached, Notes, Devices, Bits
findings.title: Older notes fail silently, and filtered counts only cover what's fetched
findings.element: Goal page › aside › Notes, goals with more than one page of notes (lists.rs load_older_notes, goal.rs notes_head)
findings.problem: When an older page fails to load, Err(_) sets done = true: Loading… disappears and the list just ends, with no error and no retry, while the head still shows the full total. The owner can't tell that notes are missing. Paging stays stopped until the goal is opened again. While pages are unfetched, a filter's N of total and the set of kind tabs reflect only what has loaded, so 3 of 300 can be far too low.
findings.principle: Visibility of system status [NNG-H1]; recognise and recover from errors [NNG-H9]
findings.fix: Add failed: bool to NoteCache. On Err, keep the notes and replace the Loading… row with Couldn't load older notes, plus a Try again link that clears failed and refetches (the fetch itself is read-only). While more is true under a filter, show the count as 3 so far of 300.

findings.unit: Goal aside: Attached, Notes, Devices, Bits
findings.title: Notes show no time
findings.element: Goal page › aside › Notes › each note (g1-notes.png)
findings.problem: A note's head gives kind, pinned and source, but not when it was written, although each note has an at value that note_order sorts by. Someone checking in through the day can't see what's new since their last look, or how old a decision is.
findings.principle: Visibility of system status [NNG-H1]; recognition rather than recall [NNG-H6]
findings.fix: Add the time to NoteItem and show it at the end of the note's head, in the format Attached uses (%b %-d, %-I:%M %p), for example Decision · pinned · you · Oct 17, 3:42 PM. Use t.muted at normal weight so the kind stays the label.

findings.unit: Goal aside: Attached, Notes, Devices, Bits
findings.title: Backlog: stray divider above N more, no way back, and cut titles with no tooltip
findings.element: Goal page › aside › Backlog, more than 5 open issues, or an issue with two pills (lists.rs line 350, goal.rs issue_piece)
findings.problem: With more than 5 open issues, the 5th row is marked last, so it draws its bottom padding and divider. N more then sits alone below that line and reads as a separate section. Once expanded, nothing collapses the list until the owner leaves the goal. Titles truncate with no tooltip, and a row with both pills leaves the title only around 90px of the 292px row, so the issue can't be read without opening it. No capture shows these states; they come from the code.
findings.principle: User control and freedom [NNG-H3]; grouped by space [SEC-2]; recognition rather than recall [NNG-H6]
findings.fix: In lists.rs, set last to k + 1 == issues.len() only, because BacklogMore already closes the section. When backlog_view is on and more than 5 issues are open, add a Show fewer link in the same place. Add .tooltip(kit::tip(title)) to the issue row, and when a row has two pills put them on a second line under the title.

findings.unit: Goal aside: Attached, Notes, Devices, Bits
findings.title: The same refs are links in some sections and plain text in others
findings.element: Goal page › aside › Bits uses (T2, G1, T3), Notes source (Finding · T1), against the Devices holder and Attached task label (g1-notes.png, g2-devices.png)
findings.problem: T2 opens the task from Devices and T8 opens it from Attached, but T2 in Bits and T1 in Notes are plain text inside a bold coloured status line, so the owner has to search for the task. The Devices holder is also a bare T2 with no word for its relation; only the tooltip gives the task's title.
findings.principle: Consistency and standards [NNG-H4]; flexibility and efficiency of use [NNG-H7]
findings.fix: Draw refs in Bits and Notes with kit::link in the mono 11px style Devices uses. T refs call m.open_task (the task's right panel) and G refs go to the goal page, which keeps one home per object. BitRow.uses needs to become a list of refs rather than a joined string, and the note's source needs the same split where it's a ref. In Devices, show In use by T2.

findings.unit: Goal aside: Attached, Notes, Devices, Bits
findings.title: A wave's files, the Bits list and the Devices list aren't virtualized
findings.element: Goal page › aside › Attached under a wave, Bits, Devices (lists.rs build)
findings.problem: The aside list makes one item per wave, so every task group and file in a wave is drawn at once, including when the kinds or waves change. Bits and Devices are each a single item too. A long goal with many evidence files per wave breaks the owner's rule, and the list has to measure one very tall item.
findings.principle: Owner rule: long lists are virtualized
findings.fix: Replace AItem::Att(k) with items per task group or file: a head, a wave label, then one item per task label and per file row, keyed with the wave, the kind and the file's id so the choice still remeasures. Do the same for Bits and Devices rows. side_piece already handles the first and last slices.

findings.unit: Goal aside: Attached, Notes, Devices, Bits
findings.title: Device state Off fails text contrast
findings.element: Goal page › aside › Devices › state label, a device that's off (pool.rs line 140)
findings.problem: Off is drawn at 12px in t.faint on t.card: #6f7a88 on #1a1f26 is 3.8:1 in dark, and #8a95a3 on #ffffff is 3.0:1 in light. Both are under 4.5:1. The label is information, not a disabled control, so the exemption doesn't apply. No capture shows it; the ratios come from theme.rs.
findings.principle: Contrast minimum [WCAG 1.4.3]
findings.fix: Use t.muted for Off: #a1abb8 is 7.1:1 in dark and #5f6b7a is 5.4:1 in light.

findings.unit: Goal aside: Attached, Notes, Devices, Bits
findings.title: The Jira On/Off control in How it runs writes a goal setting
findings.element: Goal page › aside › How it runs › Jira tickets, when Jira is on (goal.rs jira_row, set_jira_off)
findings.problem: The rest of the section is read-only, but this segmented control POSTs jira_off to the goal. That isn't one of the listed signals (start, stop, answer, idea, human-task actions), and one click changes whether new tasks ask for tickets. It isn't in the captures, so its look wasn't reviewed.
findings.principle: Owner rule: read-only apart from one-click signals; consistency and standards [NNG-H4]
findings.fix: Show it as a plain row like the others (Jira tickets: On or Off) and set it through tb. Keeping the control needs the owner's OK.

findings.title: 'Waits for you to press Start' has no Start, and reads as quiet Queued
findings.element: Projects › Tasks › T5 Upgrade the HTTP client (projects.png); also T51 and T52 in r-projects-open.png
findings.problem: T5 on the sample board tells the owner it is waiting for them, but the chip is grey Queued, it ranks near the bottom (St::Queued rank 6), adds no dot, and the row has no Start. The owner has to open the task panel to find it. Code: waits_for_start is true for manual pickup when no running goal holds the task, so T5 with no goal is real. T51 and T52 are in the extra seed and may be a seed effect, so they are not counted here.
findings.principle: Walkthrough Q2: is the correct action visible [NNG-CW]; status honesty [NNG-H1]; recognition [NNG-H6].
findings.fix: When the waiting line is the Start case, draw a small Start button in the row's meta column, posting tasks/{r}/start with mode new as home.rs Act::Start does. This is an allowed one-click signal. Have the daemon send a flag such as waits_for_start, rather than matching the text, and rank these rows with Needs in loose().

findings.title: A project with only loose tasks looks idle and never shows its task count
findings.element: Projects › project list › row for a project with 0 open goals and 1 or more open tasks
findings.problem: list() puts it in the open group, but project_row sets idle = r.open == 0, so it draws the compact muted row with no subtitle. sub()'s '2 tasks' case is tested and never drawn. The project sits among open projects looking like a 'Nothing open' one, perhaps with 'N done' on it, so its open work is easy to miss. Proven in code; no capture shows this state.
findings.principle: System status [NNG-H1]; same thing, same look [NNG-H4] [SEC-4].
findings.fix: In project_row, use let idle = r.open == 0 && r.tasks == 0, matching the partition in list(). Add a render-level test for a tasks-only project.

findings.title: A goal with every task done says Planned
findings.element: Projects › Active › G13 Replay every error, '1 of 1', full green bar (r-projects-open.png)
findings.problem: pill() has no case for all tasks done on an unfinished goal, so it falls through to Planned. The row says complete and not started at once, and the owner can't tell whether it needs closing or is about to run. R23's order would place Planned low, so the goal would also drop out of sight.
findings.principle: Match status to reality [NNG-H1]; one fact, one place [SEC-7].
findings.fix: In pill(), before the Planned fallback, add: if the total is above 0 and done equals total, return (St::Done, "All done"). Rank it with In review if it needs a human to close it. Add a case to a_goal_past_its_failed_tasks_says_in_review or a new test.

findings.title: 'Active' holds goals that are not active, and pushes Tasks and Finished out of view
findings.element: Projects › Active section heading and card (r-projects-open.png, 1360x1100)
findings.problem: The card lists Planned, Paused and Set aside goals under 'Active', and has no count, while Tasks and Finished both have one. The sidebar's ACTIVE GOALS shows 8 while webapp alone reads 12 goals, so the same word means two things. With 12 goals and 2 opened, Tasks and Finished are below the fold even at 1100 high, and the set-aside rows sit between the owner and them.
findings.principle: Consistent labels [SEC-6]; same thing, same name [NNG-H4]; rare behind [SEC-8] [NNG-PD]; group label above members (LESSONS L1).
findings.fix: Rename the heading 'Open · 12'. Fold Paused and Set aside into one row at the end of the card, 'Paused or set aside · N' with a chevron, in the same pattern as 'Nothing open', closed by default. Only started goals and up-next goals show at first.

findings.title: Goal page link is a hidden 17px target; task rows are mostly dead
findings.element: Projects › Active and Finished › G ref; Tasks › task row
findings.problem: The goal page, one of a goal's two homes, is reached here only through the G ref: 44x17px (12px text at 1.4 line height), muted, with no link look until hover, and inside a row that does something else when clicked. A near miss folds the row instead of navigating. The 17px height is under the 24px minimum and it overlaps the row target. Goal rows have no hover fill although they are clickable. Task rows are the reverse: only the ref and title respond, and the meta and chip do nothing.
findings.principle: Target size [WCAG 2.5.8]; adjacent targets [NNG-FITTS]; looks like what it is [NNG-CLICK]; hover state [NNG-H1].
findings.fix: Make the goal ref min_h(24) with items_center and show it in t.accent at rest, as kit::link does. Add .hover(bg panel_2) to goal and done rows. Move the task's on_click to the whole row with the same hover, keeping the ref and title link hover.

findings.title: Faint text fails contrast
findings.element: Projects › Finished › G ref; project list › 'N done'. Dark and light
findings.problem: t.faint text is 12px. Dark #6f7a88 gives 3.80:1 on card #1a1f26, 4.31:1 on bg #0f1216 and 3.36:1 on a selected row #232932. Light #8a95a3 gives 3.04:1 on white and about 2.84:1 on #f6f7f9. All are under 4.5:1, and these are references the owner uses to tell goals apart. Computed from theme.rs; no capture shows them.
findings.principle: Contrast [WCAG 1.4.3]
findings.fix: Use t.muted for both: #a1abb8 gives 7.1:1 on the dark card, and #5f6b7a gives 5.4:1 on white and about 5.0:1 on #f6f7f9. Keep the finished rows quiet through text_2 on the names, as they are now.

findings.title: Failed fetches look like loading forever, or like no tasks
findings.element: Projects › opened goal body and Tasks section, when GET /goals/:id or GET /tasks fails
findings.problem: app.rs keeps only Ok answers for goal details and loose tasks, and drops the Err. An opened goal then says 'Loading…' for good. Tasks simply doesn't appear while the list still says '1 task', and with no goals the pane is blank: 'No goals or tasks' needs loose to be Some. While the first answer is on its way, the Tasks section is also missing and then pops in, moving Finished.
findings.principle: Status [NNG-H1]; help recover from errors [NNG-H9]; each pane has its own loading and error state [tablet:AND-CANON].
findings.fix: Store the error by ref and for loose, as d.errs does for other fetches. Show 'Couldn't load this goal's tasks' or 'Couldn't load tasks' with a Try again link that calls m.refresh, in the same place as the rows. Show the Tasks heading with one muted 'Loading…' row while loose is None and the list's count is above 0.

findings.title: Long lists on this page are not virtualized
findings.element: Projects › Active, Tasks and Finished (Show all); project list
findings.problem: Each list is built with a for loop into a plain div, so every row is laid out on every draw. Show all puts every finished goal in, Tasks has no limit, and opened goals add their tasks. Finished only grows. This breaks the owner's rule, and Backlog, Needs you and Releases already use virtual lists. Effect on speed was not measured.
findings.principle: Owner rule: long lists virtualized. Responsiveness [mobile:NNG-RESPONSE].
findings.fix: Flatten the main pane into a line enum (Head, SectionLabel, GoalRow, TaskRow, DoneRow, ShowAll) and render it through gpui_kit::list as backlog.rs does, drawing card edges per line. Same for the project list when it can pass about 50 rows.

findings.title: Opened goals don't group tasks by wave, and wave wording is unclear
findings.element: Projects › Active › opened goal › task rows, e.g. G2's T8-T11 (r-projects-open.png)
findings.problem: Tasks are sorted by wave, but the wave is named only in the meta of some open rows: T9 says 'wave 2', T8 says 'for 1h 5m', T11 is blank and done rows say nothing. The owner can't see where one wave ends, while the goal row says 'wave 2'. T10's 'Waits for wave 2 to start T9' is also hard to parse.
findings.principle: Group label above members, members indented (LESSONS L1); proximity [NNG-PROX]; plain words [NNG-H2].
findings.fix: When a goal has more than one wave, draw a small 'Wave 2' label row above each wave's tasks in goal_tasks and drop the 'wave N' case from task_meta. Reword the daemon line in waitsfor.rs, e.g. 'Waits for T9 to start'.

findings.title: The no-projects state is a dead end
findings.element: Projects › no projects (r-empty-projects.png)
findings.problem: 'No projects' sits in 13px muted text near the top of the right pane, with an empty 280px list beside it. It doesn't say how a project gets onto the board. The page is read-only, so the owner has nothing to act on and no hint where to go next. It is rare for the owner, hence 2.
findings.principle: Empty states need a way forward [mobile:NNG-EMPTY]; help in context [NNG-H10].
findings.fix: When there are no rows, drop the list column and centre one block in the page: 'No projects yet', then one line naming how a project appears (confirm the real route first; it was not found in this review). No button is needed, so the read-only rule stands.

findings.title: After Start, the app says 'Started' but shows nothing starting or what comes next
findings.element: Goal page › toast, status bar, queued rows; Sidebar › new row (r-g7-started.png, g2-more-started.png)
findings.problem: The toast says 'Started: 2 tasks queued', but nothing has started. The bar stays the same grey because queued and planned look alike, 0 terminals are in use, and T67 has no line saying why it hasn't begun. The new sidebar row for G7 has an empty bar and no time, while every other row shows one. In g2-more-started.png T9 and T11 are Queued with no reason, with 1 of 3 terminals in use. That missing reason may come from the sample's Midna being down; the rest doesn't.
findings.principle: Cognitive walkthrough Q4: after the action, users see progress toward the goal [NNG-CW] [NNG-H1]
findings.fix: Change the toast to '2 tasks queued' and keep 'Started' for when a task goes to working. Give queued bar segments their own tint: t.accent at about 35% against the planned grey. Give the next-up row a line such as 'Next: starts when a terminal is free' when waiting_line returns null. Set last_update when a goal is run so the sidebar shows 'just now'.

findings.title: Blocker toasts vanish after 3 seconds
findings.element: Toast after goal-run or goal-run-now when tasks can't start
findings.problem: with_waits can append up to two blocker sentences plus 'N more wait', such as 'T192 waits for you to do H197', but ok toasts stay only 3s (TOAST_OK) at bottom centre, far from the top-right button. That is the one message that tells the owner to act, and it gets the same time as 'Paused'.
findings.principle: Users need enough time to read; status stays visible [NNG-H1] [WCAG 2.2.1]
findings.fix: Keep the toast for 6s when `waiting` is non-empty, or until dismissed. Scale the time with length, about 1s per 15 characters, with a 3s minimum.

findings.title: Start at has no label or time preview, and it covers the status readout
findings.element: Goal page › Start at popover (g2-start-at.png)
findings.problem: The popover holds a field whose only label is a placeholder ('5pm, tomorrow 9am'), which disappears on typing. The owner can't see how the typed time was read until after it is scheduled, and a wrongly read time on a job that spends agents is costly. On a part-run goal nothing says only the planned task is affected. The popover opens at the click point minus 240px, so it hides '2 of 7' and sits detached from the button.
findings.principle: Visible label; constraints stated up front; error prevention [WCAG 3.3.2] [NNG-H5]
findings.fix: Add a visible label above the field: 'Start the planned tasks at', or 'Start 1 more task at' on a part-run goal. Under the field show the parsed time live, such as 'Tomorrow at 9 AM'; this needs a check mode on the at path, or an app-side parse. Anchor the popover to the split button's bottom-right edge, at the button's rect instead of e.position().

findings.title: Scheduled and work-hours times break the AM/PM rule
findings.element: Header buttons, tooltips, toasts, placeholder, footer pill (r-g12.png, r-g6-hours-menu.png)
findings.problem: 'Starts tomorrow at 1:55am' and 'Waiting until tomorrow 3am' use lowercase am with no space, on the same screens as '6:25 PM'. The doc comment on scheduled_at even promises '5 PM'. The same moment also appears three ways: 'tomorrow 3am', 'tomorrow at 3am' and 'Sat 3am'.
findings.principle: Owner rule: 12-hour times with AM/PM; same thing, same form [NNG-H4]
findings.fix: Change fmt::clock12 to return '3 AM' and '1:55 AM', which also covers day_clock and opens_at. Use 'tomorrow at 3 AM' on the wait button too. Change the placeholder to '5 PM, tomorrow 9 AM' after confirming parse_at accepts that form. Update the tests that pin the old strings.

findings.title: The button tooltip stays on top of the menu it opened
findings.element: Start caret and wait button menus (r-g7-start-menu.png, r-g6-hours-menu.png)
findings.problem: With the menu open, the tooltip stays drawn over it. In r-g6-hours-menu.png it clips the top of the first item, 'Start now', and hides part of the goal title and the button. In r-g7-start-menu.png it covers 'Open in Claude'. It repeats what the menu already says.
findings.principle: Keep the task in view; extra content must not obscure the control [NNG-H8] [WCAG 1.4.13]
findings.fix: Hide the tooltip while the button's menu is open: skip .tooltip when m.menu_open(id) is set, or clear the active tooltip in toggle_menu. Also open the menu from the button's edge rather than the pointer.

findings.title: How it runs disagrees with the waves and bar beside it
findings.element: Goal page › How it runs › Order and Terminals (goal-g2.png)
findings.problem: Order says 'Side by side', but the cards beside it say Wave 3 runs 'After wave 2' and T10 waits for wave 2. how_runs drops waves whenever run_in_order is off. So the owner can't predict what runs next, which is the point of this card. Terminals says '1 in use' while the status line says '2 working', because how_runs skips shared tasks and progress counts them.
findings.principle: One fact, one place; the copies must not disagree [SEC-7] [NNG-H1]
findings.fix: Return 'Side by side, by wave' for (false, true) in how_runs, if waves still gate there. For Terminals, count shared tasks too or say so: '3 at most · 1 in use · 1 from another goal'.

findings.title: 'Waits for wave 2 to start T9' reads backwards
findings.element: Goal page › Wave 3 › T10 wait line (goal-g2.png, g2-more-started.png)
findings.problem: The line sits on T10 in Wave 3 but names T9, in a different wave, as the thing being started. It reads as though T10 will start T9, or as though wave 2 has a job the owner must do. The owner can't tell whether to wait or act.
findings.principle: Plain language in the user's words [NNG-H2]
findings.fix: In waves::hold_reason, use 'Waits for wave 2: T9 hasn't started yet'. Update the tests that pin the string.

findings.title: Pause's banner and toast leave out that PRs wait too
findings.element: Goal page › Paused banner and toast; wait and Start menu Pause rows (g2-paused.png, r-g6-hours-menu.png)
findings.problem: The Pause tooltip says PRs wait for fixes, comments and merges, and prflow::goal_paused enforces that. The banner, toast and menu sublines only say 'Nothing new starts… running tasks carry on'. A goal with open PRs goes quiet, and the status that stays on screen never explains why.
findings.principle: Visibility of system status [NNG-H1]
findings.fix: Pass `reviewing` into gate_view and the toast. When true, the banner says 'Nothing new starts and PRs wait for fixes, comments and merges. Tasks already running carry on.' The toast says 'Paused. PRs wait too; running tasks carry on.'

findings.title: Rows can say 'press Start' on a goal that has no Start button
findings.element: Goal page › header against queued rows, queued-only never-run goal (r-g6-hours-menu.png)
findings.problem: The wording in this capture is a seed effect: waits_for_start is true for manual pickup in a goal with no ran_at. The button gap is real logic, though. run_buttons_view shows Start only with planned tasks, or when paused or unstarted, so a queued-only goal gets 'Waiting until…' or Pause. The tooltip says the tasks start when work hours open, but waiting_line checks waits_for_start before hours, so they would not. In work hours there would be no route to Start on the page. Whether real goals reach this state wasn't proven.
findings.principle: Cognitive walkthrough Q2: the correct action is visible; no dead ends [NNG-CW] [NNG-H3]
findings.fix: Have the goal payload report whether any task waits for Start, and show the primary Start button in that case. Otherwise, if the state can't occur in production, make the daemon rule that out and leave the UI alone.

findings.title: The sidebar sorts by age, so attention can sit below the fold
findings.element: Sidebar › Active goals (r-g7.png, g2-more-started.png, g2-resumed.png)
findings.problem: Rows sort by id, newest first, and about five and a half fit at this height. Open goal G2 is out of view in g2-more-started.png, so the owner can't watch the row update after pressing Start. G1, the goal with the needs-you dot in goal-g2.png, sorts last, and the last visible row is cut by the footer. The primary task is seeing which goals need attention; the Needs you count is the workaround.
findings.principle: Primary content first; frequent in view [SEC-8] [SCR-2] [NNG-H6]
findings.fix: Sort needs-you and stopped goals first, then the rest newest first, in active_goals. Scroll the open goal's row into view on navigation. Keep the list a virtualized scroller if it grows, per the owner's rule.

findings.title: A failure the owner went past looks the same as one still waiting
findings.element: Goal page › Wave 1 and Wave 2, r-g4-continue.png; Goals › G4 row
findings.problem: After 'Continue anyway', the gate goes, but Wave 1 still reads 'A task failed' with a red dot, and Wave 2 reads 'After wave 1', as if it still waits on it. `now_line` and `next_line` never read `passed`, so the Goals row keeps red '1 failed · T54 failed' for the rest of the goal. The owner keeps seeing an alarm for something already decided, and can't tell a handled failure from a live one on that row. The sidebar drops the sign, so the surfaces disagree.
findings.principle: Visibility of system status [NNG-H1]; one fact, one reading [SEC-7]
findings.fix: When `passed` is true on a failed wave, set the head meta to 'T54 failed · went on anyway' with a muted dot. Have Wave 2 read 'Next' or 'Now', not 'After wave 1'. In `now_line`, leave out failures in passed waves so the row shows the live state, and keep the red part of the bar as the record.

findings.title: Stopped goals are quieter in the sidebar than questions, and can sit below the fold
findings.element: Sidebar › Active goals, r-needs.png, 1360×860, dark
findings.problem: The orange dot appears only when `needs > 0`, so G1 has one but stopped G3 and G4 don't. Their only sign is 11px muted text. The list sorts by id, not by attention, so at 860 high G3's line is cut off under the footer and G2 and G1 are out of view (r-needs.png). The sidebar shows far less at this height than at 1240.
findings.principle: Frequent in view, rare behind [SEC-8]; Visibility of system status [NNG-H1]
findings.fix: In `render`, show `kit::dot(t.warn, 7.)` when `i(g,"needs") > 0` or the goal has a `stopped` line or held wave, and `t.down` for a failed one. Sort `active_goals` with waiting-on-you first, then newest. Colour the 'stopped for you' part of the sub line `t.warn_fg`.

findings.title: A missed outcome reads Done on the Goals row and full green in the sidebar
findings.element: Goals › G13 row; Sidebar › G13; Goal page r-g13.png
findings.problem: Needs you says '2 missed · Holds the goal' and the goal page says 'Outcome not met · 2 misses', while the Goals row says 'Done' and the sidebar shows '1 of 1' on a full green bar (r-goals.png). The row also offers Pause on a goal with nothing left to pause, a control the goal page doesn't show. A glance at either surface says this goal is finished when it is held open.
findings.principle: Consistency and standards [NNG-H4]; one fact, one place [SEC-7]
findings.fix: In `now_line`/`goal_row`, when `misses > 0` and nothing is active, show 'Outcome not met' in St::Needs with next '2 misses hold the goal'. Make `action` None there. In `goal_sub`, show '1 of 1 · 2 misses', and draw the sidebar dot.

findings.title: A held wave doesn't say who held it, when or why
findings.element: Goal page › Wave 2 › gate, r-g5.png, dark, held wave
findings.problem: 'Wave 2 is held.' repeats the header's 'Held' and gives nothing to decide with. Agents and the CLI can hold a wave as well as the owner, so 'Let wave 2 start' may undo a hold someone placed on purpose. `held_at` is already in the wave's JSON, and the holder is logged as an event.
findings.principle: Help users diagnose [NNG-H9]; walkthrough question 1, will users try the right thing [NNG-CW]
findings.fix: Add `held_by` to the wave JSON from the 'held wave N' event. Change the text to 'Claude held wave 2 at 4:12 PM. T57 waits.' using the 12-hour format. An optional reason on `tb goal wave --hold` could follow, shown as a second line.

findings.title: Continue on Needs you and Goals skips the look the stop asks for
findings.element: Needs you › Checkout on mobile row; Goals › G3 row
findings.problem: The stop exists so the owner looks at wave 1 first, and the gate says 'Look it over'. The Goals row gives bare 'Continue' as the page's only blue button, and the Needs you row offers it with no summary. Neither says what it starts, and neither shows what the wave produced. `stop_vm` builds '2 tasks wait in wave 2' and the review line, but r-needs.png shows neither. The title link to the goal has no link look. There's no undo on these surfaces.
findings.principle: Walkthrough question 3, does the label match the result [NNG-CW]; Error prevention [NNG-H5]
findings.fix: Keep it one click, per the owner's rule. Label both buttons 'Continue to wave 2', as the gate does. Add a 'Review wave 1' link beside it that opens the goal at that wave, and on the Goals row make Continue the secondary look when this link is present.

findings.title: The gate's confirmation note never shows, and toasts don't name the goal
findings.element: Goal page after release, r-g3-continue.png, r-g4-continue.png, r-g5-start.png; toast in r-goals-continue.png and r-needs-continue.png
findings.problem: `continue_wave` sends its success text to the `wgate:G` note with toast off, and that note is drawn only inside `gate_el`, which is gone once the wave releases. The three post-release gate captures show no message. The gate just vanishes and the rows reflow. Elsewhere the toast says 'The goal goes on' without saying which goal or what starts.
findings.principle: Visibility of system status [NNG-H1]; Status messages [WCAG 4.1.3]
findings.fix: Pass `toast: true` with `grp: None` on success in `continue_wave`, keeping the inline note for errors. Use one message on all three surfaces: 'G3: wave 2 can start', or 'G4: went on past T54'.

findings.title: 'Stopped' means different things, and a review stop has about five names
findings.element: Sidebar sub line; Goals row; Needs you group names; goal page
findings.problem: One review stop reads 'stopped for you', 'Stopped for your review', 'wave 1 finished', 'Done · waiting for your review' and 'Wave 1 is done'. Needs you has its own 'Stopped' group for closed terminals (`Kind::Stopped`), yet a goal the sidebar calls stopped is filed under Decide. Looking under Stopped for a stopped goal finds nothing.
findings.principle: Consistency and standards [NNG-H4]; Match the real world [NNG-H2]
findings.fix: Pick one word per kind and use it everywhere: 'Ready for review', 'Failed', 'Held'. Sidebar: '2 of 4 · ready for review'. Goals row: 'Ready for review'. Needs you: 'Checkout on mobile · wave 1 ready for review'. Keep 'Stopped' for closed terminals only.

findings.title: On a goal with many waves the gate can be off screen, and the page top doesn't mention it
findings.element: Goal page › header and progress line, r-g3.png; a long goal such as G6 (9 waves)
findings.problem: The header and progress line say only '2 of 4 done · 2 queued' at a review stop. The sole sign is the gate inside the wave's card. With short goals it's in view, but on a 9-wave goal a stop at a later wave likely sits below the fold, and the top of the page gives no hint. `goal_status` already computes 'Waiting on you', but no capture shows it drawn on this page. No long-goal capture exists, so this is inferred.
findings.principle: Visibility of system status [NNG-H1]; Focus on what the page is for [SCR-1]
findings.fix: Add the stop to the progress line, as 'Outcome not met' already does: 'Stopped at wave 3' in warn colour (red for a failure), clicking scrolls the virtualized list to `goal-wave-w3`. Or scroll to the gate when the page opens on a stopped goal.

findings.title: Second lines repeat or read oddly
findings.element: Goals › rows and task lines (r-goals.png, r-goals-open.png)
findings.problem: G4 reads '1 failed' then 'T54 failed'. '1 task in wave 3' doesn't say it comes next. T10's 'Waits for wave 2 to start T9' (waves.rs:127) reads as if wave 2 must start T9, and it sits under a header that already says 'After wave 2'.
findings.principle: One fact, one place [SEC-7]; Match with the real world [NNG-H2]
findings.fix: For a failure, make the second line the task's title or reason. Write 'Then 1 task in wave 3'. Drop the wave waiting line when the wave header already says it.

findings.title: One age column mixes three kinds of time
findings.element: Goals › open row › task age column (r-goals-expand-all.png)
findings.problem: The same column shows 'now', 'under a minute', '1h 5m' and '7:56 PM': time since asking, elapsed run time and clock time, with no way to tell them apart, and 'now' and 'under a minute' side by side.
findings.principle: Consistency [NNG-H4]
findings.fix: Map 'under a minute' to 'now' in short(), and let the status chip explain the rest. If it still confuses, prefix finished times with 'at'.

findings.title: Filter menu opens at the pointer, not at the button
findings.element: Goals › header › project filter (r-goals-filter-menu.png)
findings.problem: project_filter places the menu from the click position, so it starts about 43 image px right of the button's left edge, and the spot changes with where you click.
findings.principle: Alignment [SCR-4]; platform pop-up behaviour [HIG-MACOS]
findings.fix: Anchor the menu to the button's bounds: left edge aligned, 4px below.

findings.title: Empty state is bare and off the page's left edge
findings.element: Goals › no goals (r-empty.png)
findings.problem: 'No goals' floats centred under a left-aligned title on a blank page, and doesn't say how goals appear in a read-only app.
findings.principle: Designed empty states with a way forward [mobile:NNG-EMPTY]
findings.fix: Left-align it to the 28px page edge and say what happens: 'No goals yet. Goals your agents start show up here.'

findings.title: '2 working' and '1 in use' disagree
findings.element: Progress line and How it runs › Terminals, goal-g2.png
findings.problem: The progress line counts the shared T2 and Terminals doesn't, because how_runs reads tasks and progress reads counted(). It's explainable, but looks like a bug on first read.
findings.principle: One fact, one place [SEC-7]
findings.fix: Optional: when shared tasks are running, show '3 at most · 1 in use · 1 shared'.

findings.title: The split button shows no busy state for menu actions
findings.element: Header › Start button and caret (goal.rs lines 961-971)
findings.problem: Start now and Start at use their own busy keys, but the main button only checks goal-run and the caret is never disabled. While those requests run, the button stays live with no feedback, and a second Start can be sent.
findings.principle: Visibility of system status [NNG-H1]
findings.fix: Optional: treat goal-run-now and goal-at as busy for the split button, as sched-menu already does, and disable the caret too.

findings.title: 'Deprioritized' is a heavier word than the app's own 'set aside'
findings.element: Gate banner, r-g9.png, and the row reason 'Its goal is deprioritized'
findings.problem: The API and Home code call this 'set aside', and the banner's button says 'Bring it back', but the label on screen is 'Deprioritized'.
findings.principle: Match between the system and the real world [NNG-H2]
findings.fix: Optional: label the banner 'Set aside' and the row reason 'Its goal is set aside'.

findings.title: Typing 'cancel' in Start at may report 'Scheduled'
findings.element: Goal › Start at popover › schedule_goal
findings.problem: The daemon's is_off treats off, none, cancel and clear as dropping the schedule, but the client checks only for exactly 'off'. If the route uses is_off, typing 'cancel' removes the schedule and the toast falls back to 'Scheduled'.
findings.principle: Commands never report success they didn't have [NNG-H1]
findings.fix: Have the toast read the response: if it has no start_at, say 'G12 isn't scheduled any more'.

findings.title: 'Waits for you to press Start' has no Start nearby, mostly a seed effect
findings.element: Goal page › queued rows T60–T66 and page header, extra seed (r-g6.png)
findings.problem: Code check: the line needs pickup=manual and a goal with no ran_at (or a line session), so seven rows of it come from the seed, and this is not rated as a normal-use defect. Two real effects remain on that path. waiting_line checks it before the goal's wave blocker, so wave 9 would say press Start while wave 8 hasn't run. And run_buttons_view shows Start only for planned tasks or a paused goal, so the header offers none.
findings.principle: Will users notice the correct action [NNG-CW]
findings.fix: In waiting_line, check runner::goal_blocker before waits_for_start, so later waves show what holds them. Say where the button is, or show Start in run_buttons_view when any queued task has waits_for_start true.

findings.title: The unlabeled age column mixes meanings and overflows
findings.element: Goal page › task row › age cell (goal-g2.png, g1.png)
findings.problem: One column shows a finish time ('6:17 PM'), a run length ('1h 5m', 'under a minute') and time since asking ('now'). 'under a minute' is about 80px in a 44px cell and spills about 24px into the PR cell. A long PR value such as 'PR #401 · In review' or a branch would likely collide with it for that first minute (not seen).
findings.principle: Alignment [SCR-4]; consistency [NNG-H4]
findings.fix: Use '<1m' for age in status::row, leaving fmt::span alone for the panel, and widen the cell to 56px.

findings.title: The Queued chip disappears on row hover in dark mode
findings.element: Goal page › task row hover, wave 8 row T65 (r-g6.png)
findings.problem: Row hover uses panel_2 (#232932) and the Queued chip fill is seg (#232931), one step apart, so the chip's shape vanishes under the pointer and the text floats.
findings.principle: Looks like what it is [WCAG 1.4.11, as polish: the label text remains]
findings.fix: Use t.tint for the row hover, or give the Queued and Stopped chips a 1px t.border_2 edge as Planned has.

findings.title: The panel's '3 of 6' reads like progress
findings.element: Task panel › header chip 'Wave 2 · 3 of 6' (g2-task-panel.png)
findings.problem: Behind the panel the goal says '2 of 7' done. The chip's '3 of 6' is T8's position in the goal, but the two look like competing progress figures.
findings.principle: One fact, one place [SEC-7]; match with the real world [NNG-H2]
findings.fix: Change goal_chip to 'Wave 2 · task 3 of 6', or drop the position and keep 'Wave 2'.

findings.unit: Goal aside: Attached, Notes, Devices, Bits
findings.title: Two pop-up buttons with two looks, and Notes filters a third way
findings.element: Goal page › aside › Attached kinds button and wave picker, Notes kind tabs (goal-g2.png, g1-notes.png)
findings.problem: All kinds is a 12px borderless button. The wave picker right below it is a 13px semibold bordered box whose -6px margin pushes its border 6px past the section's edge. Notes narrows by kind with a segmented control and no counts, while Attached does the same job with a menu that has counts.
findings.principle: One look per role [SEC-4]; alignment [SCR-4]
findings.fix: Drop the -6px margin on wave_btn so its border lines up with the section edges. Use menu_btn for the Notes kind choice too, placed left of Hide, with the same counts as the Attached kinds menu. This also saves the tab row's height.

findings.unit: Goal aside: Attached, Notes, Devices, Bits
findings.title: Menus open from the click point, and the wave tooltip lands on the open menu
findings.element: Goal page › aside › Attached › wave menu and kinds menu (g2-wave-menu.png, g2-att-kinds.png)
findings.problem: Both menus sit at the click position minus 150px, so they land somewhere different each time, and a click at the picker's left end pushes the wave menu over the wave cards. The kinds menu covers the wave picker. A Wave 2 tooltip repeats the button's own label and floats over the open menu.
findings.principle: Consistency and standards [NNG-H4]; aesthetic and minimalist design [NNG-H8]
findings.fix: Anchor each menu to its button's bounds: wave menu left-aligned to the picker and as wide as it, kinds menu right-aligned to its button. Show the picker's tooltip only when the label is truncated, and never while its menu is open.

findings.unit: Goal aside: Attached, Notes, Devices, Bits
findings.title: How it runs: tautological wording and an unexplained in-use count
findings.element: Goal page › aside › How it runs (g1-notes.png, r-g13.png, goal-g2.png)
findings.problem: Order: In order says nothing. On G2 the section says 1 in use while the header says 2 working, because in_use counts only the goal's own tasks and T2 comes from another goal. Review stop After wave 3 also repeats the pill on the wave 3 card.
findings.principle: Match with the real world [NNG-H2]; one fact, one place [SEC-7]
findings.fix: Change In order to One at a time. Change the terminals value to 1 in use here when the goal has shared tasks working.

findings.title: The status column doesn't hold together
findings.element: Projects › Active › opened goal rows, dark (r-projects-open.png; projects.png)
findings.problem: The Queued chip's fill (#232931) equals the open-goal background (#232932), so Queued loses its pill shape there while Done and Working keep theirs. Goal pills are 96px and task chips 104px in the same column, and the meta column starts left of the bar column.
findings.principle: One look per role [SEC-4]; aligned to a grid [SCR-4] [NNG-GRID].
findings.fix: Use one width, 104px, for both. Give Queued a 1px border_2 line, as Planned has one, or use a fill one step lighter on panel_2.

findings.title: Long names cut off with no full text; rows stretch; dates have no year
findings.element: Projects › Active › G6 (r-projects-open.png); projects-main; Finished › date
findings.problem: G6's name is cut at 'so the wh…' and neither opening the row nor hovering shows the rest. projects-main has no max width, unlike Backlog's 1320, so name and pill drift apart on a large display. Finished dates use '%b %-d', which is ambiguous after a year.
findings.principle: Recognition [NNG-H6]; content has max widths [tablet:AND-T2].
findings.fix: Add a tooltip with the full name on truncated rows. Set max_w(px(1320.)) on main's content. Add the year to dates outside the current year: 'Oct 18, 2025'.

findings.title: Decide's count doesn't match its visible rows
findings.element: Needs you › Decide header, r-needs.png
findings.problem: 'DECIDE 3' sits above two rows, and 'DECIDE 2' above one after Continue (r-needs-continue.png). It counts items by design, with '2 missed' folded into one row, so it adds up only after working it out.
findings.principle: Consistency and standards [NNG-H4]
findings.fix: Count rows in the header, or leave it as is if the owner prefers items.

what_works: Goals page: The row's three columns (what it is, how far along, what it's doing now) read fast, and aligned bars make scanning easy at 1360 and 1728 wide.
Goals page: Continue is the single filled button, so a goal stopped for review stands out and the action is right there.
Goals page: Opening in place keeps context: wave headers say when and why ('Done · waiting for your review', 'After wave 1'), and tasks open in the right panel, which keeps to one home per object.
Goals page: The roomy Paused shelf (goals-both-paused.png) uses spare space well, with each goal's purpose under its name.
Goals page: Both themes hold together: muted text passes on cards and bands (5.06:1 light on page background, 7.12:1 dark on card), and times use 12-hour AM/PM.
Goal run state and buttons: The review stop gate is the model for the others: it says what happened, what to do and what happens next, and the button names the result ('Continue to wave 2').

Goal run state and buttons: Button labels follow the run state closely: 'Start 1 more task', 'Start tomorrow: 1 more task' and 'Starts tomorrow at 1:55am' each say what will really happen, and tooltips cover the PR follow-ups a pause holds.

Goal run state and buttons: Composition holds across sizes and themes from 1360 up: the waves dominate, How it runs stays quiet, and light and dark read the same (goal-g2.png, g2-light.png, g2-large.png).
Goal run state and buttons: The owner's lessons are kept: Attached uses a pop-up for waves (L2) and puts the task caption above its indented files (L1).
Goal run state and buttons: Fixes above stay within the owner's rules: each new control is a one-click signal, so none needs the owner's OK for a rule change.
Goal header and menus: One blue primary action per header, with the state in the button itself: 'Start 1 more task', 'Starts tomorrow…', 'Waiting until…'. The label says what happens next.
Goal header and menus: Menu rows pair a bold action with a one-line consequence ('Nothing new starts; running tasks carry on'), which suits one-click signals.
Goal header and menus: Start at's flow is sound: the field opens focused, Enter submits, Esc cancels and returns focus, and errors appear in the popover in plain words.
Goal header and menus: The Attached wave picker is a pop-up rather than tabs (L2), and T8's files sit indented under their task label (L1). Light theme holds up well in r-g3-light.png.
Goal waves and lists: Wave cards follow a clear order, with state, time and review stop in one header line, and the review stop is announced ahead of time on the wave it follows.
Goal waves and lists: Lessons hold: Attached uses a pop-up for waves (L2) and puts 'T8 Batch the session writes' above its indented files (L1).
Goal waves and lists: Both lists are virtualized per row and keep their scroll place when items change, and times use 12-hour AM/PM.
Goal waves and lists: Task chips use one colour language across the status bar, rows and sidebar, and the panel opens without losing the page behind it.
Goal waves and lists: Finding details open inline with room to read, and the read-only rule is kept: the signals on these surfaces are single clicks.

Goal aside: Attached, Notes, Devices, Bits: L2 is met: waves use a pop-up menu that scrolls at 360px, with each wave's phase and count. Notes keeps a segmented control only for a fixed set of at most four kinds, so L2 isn't broken there.
Goal aside: Attached, Notes, Devices, Bits: L1 is met for tasks: the ref and title sit above the files, which are indented, and the label opens the task in the right panel.
Goal aside: Attached, Notes, Devices, Bits: Sections with nothing to show disappear rather than showing filler, and the aside stays quiet beside the wave cards.
Goal aside: Attached, Notes, Devices, Bits: Attached opens on the wave in progress, and the wave and kind choices don't reset each other. Menu rows that hold nothing are dimmed and inert.
Goal aside: Attached, Notes, Devices, Bits: Times in the Attached file details use the 12-hour format with AM/PM, as the owner's rule asks.
Projects page: The layout is calm and scans quickly: one list, one header, cards with a fixed column for progress and status, and orange reserved for what needs the owner.
Projects page: Goals open in place while tasks open in the right panel and goals keep their page, so the one-home rule holds; the Nothing open fold keeps the picked project in view.
Projects page: Text plus a bar for progress ('2 of 6 · wave 2') and a labelled pill mean goal status does not rely on colour alone.
Projects page: Times and metadata stay spare: no filler labels, and the header shows only what the project has (release, waits-for and backlog facts).
Flow 2: Run a goal: A planned goal has one clear blue action, and after Start the header drops to Pause and Open in Claude, so the button set always matches the state (r-g7.png, r-g7-started.png).
Flow 2: Run a goal: The Paused banner is hard to miss, and each held row explains itself with 'Its goal is paused' (g2-paused.png).
Flow 2: Run a goal: 'Start 1 more task' says exactly how much it will do, and T68's 'Waits for T67 to finish first' makes order visible.
Flow 2: Run a goal: A scheduled goal swaps the primary Start for a quiet button that states the time and holds Start now, Change the time and Cancel (r-g12.png).

Flow 3: Wave stop: The review stop is the model to copy: it is noticed on all three surfaces, it releases from all three, and each surface clears straight after (r-goals-continue.png, r-needs-continue.png, r-g3-continue.png).

Flow 3: Wave stop: The goal-page gates are clear and sit at the wave they belong to. Amber against red separates a pause from a failure, and each button names its result ('Continue to wave 2', 'Let wave 2 start').
Flow 3: Wave stop: Keeping stops under Decide leaves 'Agents waiting' honest: its heading and count mean exactly what they say.
Flow 3: Wave stop: The Goals row's now and next lines give a stopped goal a clear state at a glance, with 'Wave 1 done · 2 tasks in wave 2' as a good example.
Flow 3: Wave stop: Times use 12-hour AM/PM throughout, and labels carry no filler.
